title: Why Your Refrigerator Compressor is Getting Hot

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• What Does the Compressor Do in a Refrigerator?
• +
How Dirty Refrigerator Condenser Coils Lead to a Hot Compressor
• +
How a Faulty Refrigerator Thermostat Leads to a Hot Compressor
• +
How a Faulty Refrigerator Condenser Fan Motor Leads to a Hot Compressor
• +
How an Overloaded Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
• +
How Low Voltage Supply to a Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
• How a Poorly Positioned Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
• How Low Refrigerant Levels Lead to a Hot Compressor
It's normal for your refrigerator compressor to be warm, however, if it's very hot then there is likely a problem that needs to be addressed. A hot compressor is typically caused by dirty condenser coils, a malfunctioning fan motor, a faulty thermostat, or low refrigerant levels. It can also be caused by something as simple as overloading the fridge with groceries or placing the fridge too close to the wall. Understanding the root causes of a hot compressor is essential to maintaining your refrigerator’s efficiency and longevity. In this article, we'll explore the common reasons behind a hot refrigerator compressor, and practical step-by-step solutions to help you resolve the issue, and ensure your refrigerator runs smoothly and keeps your food fresh.

sections.heading: What Does the Compressor Do in a Refrigerator?
sections.text:
The compressor is a crucial part of the refrigeration cycle, which is the process whereby heat is removed from inside the refrigerator to keep it cool. The compressor pressurizes the refrigerant gas, which is converted into a liquid when it passes through the condenser coils. The liquid evaporates and absorbs heat from the interior of the fridge and cools it down. The cooled air is then circulated throughout the refrigerator to keep the food items cold. The gas returns to the compressor where it begins this cycle again. In summary, the compressor is responsible for pressurizing and circulating the refrigerant throughout the refrigeration system and facilitating the removal of heat from inside the refrigerator to the outside environment.
If the compressor overheats, it may be unable to compress refrigerant gas effectively, resulting in reduced cooling capacity and longer cooling cycles. It will also consume more energy as it struggles to maintain the desired temperature inside the refrigerator. This can lead to higher electricity bills and unnecessary energy use. Furthermore, overheating over a long period of time can damage the internal components of the compressor, such as the motor windings, and electrical connections. Over time, this can lead to premature compressor failure and the need for costly repairs. If the compressor continues to overheat, it may eventually fail completely. A failed compressor can cause the entire refrigeration system to stop working, leaving your refrigerator unable to function at all. Therefore, if you notice that your compressor is getting hotter than usual, you should address this promptly.

sections.heading: How Dirty Refrigerator Condenser Coils Lead to a Hot Compressor
sections.text: The condenser coils are designed to release heat generated from inside the refrigerator. When these coils are covered in dust, dirt, or debris, they will be unable to carry out this function efficiently and the overall temperature of the refrigeration system increases. As a result, the compressor has to work harder and run more frequently to maintain the desired internal temperature. Over time, this constant strain can cause the compressor to overheat, increase energy costs, and lower the overall efficiency of the refrigerator.

sections.heading: How to Clean Condenser Coils to Fix a Hot Compressor
sections.text:
1. Before you begin cleaning, unplug the refrigerator from the power outlet to avoid electric shock.
2. You can typically find the condenser coil either on the back of the refrigerator or underneath the door behind a grille.
3. If the coils are at the bottom, you may need to remove the access panel or grille covering them. This may involve unscrewing a few screws or simply snapping off the grille, depending on your refrigerator model.
4. Once you have access to the coils, use a coil cleaning brush or a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment to remove any dirt or debris. Be careful to avoid damaging the coils.
5. For any hard-to-reach areas where dust may accumulate, you can use a narrow brush or a can of compressed air to reach these areas.
6. Once the coils are clean and you've inspected them for damage, reassemble any panels or grilles you removed and plug the refrigerator back into the power outlet.

sections.heading: How a Faulty Refrigerator Thermostat Leads to a Hot Compressor
sections.text: The thermostat is designed to monitor the internal temperature of the refrigerator and signal the compressor to turn on or off to maintain the correct temperature. If the thermostat is faulty, it may not accurately read the temperature inside the refrigerator. It may continuously signal the compressor to run even if the temperature is already at the desired level. When the compressor runs continuously without the necessary breaks, it can lead to the compressor becoming extremely hot as it is constantly working to cool down the refrigerator. You will need to replace the refrigerator thermostat to restore the proper functioning of your appliance.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Thermostat to Fix a Hot Compressor
sections.text:
1. Unplug the refrigerator from the power outlet to ensure your safety.
2. The thermostat is typically located behind the control panel inside the refrigerator compartment. Refer to your refrigerator's user manual to locate the thermostat.
3. Depending on the model, you may need to remove the control panel to access the thermostat. This usually involves unscrewing a few screws and gently prying off the panel. Be careful not to damage any wires or components.
4. Carefully disconnect the wires connected to it. Take note of where each wire is connected or take a picture for reference later.
5. Use a multimeter to test the thermostat for continuity. If it shows no continuity at its coldest setting, it may be defective and needs replacement.
6. Unscrew the thermostat from its mounting bracket or housing. Keep track of the screws and any other fasteners.
7. Position the new thermostat in place and secure it with the screws. Make sure it's properly aligned and seated in the mounting bracket.
8. Reconnect the wires to the corresponding terminals on the new thermostat. Double-check that each wire is securely connected and in the correct position.
9. If you removed the control panel, carefully reattach it to the refrigerator. Secure any screws or fasteners to ensure it's firmly in place.
10. Plug the refrigerator back into the power outlet and turn it on. Test the thermostat to ensure it's working properly.

sections.heading: How a Faulty Refrigerator Condenser Fan Motor Leads to a Hot Compressor
sections.text: The condenser fan motor is responsible for cooling the condenser coils and the compressor by circulating air over them, which helps diffuse the heat generated during the refrigeration cycle. If the condenser fan motor fails or operates inefficiently, it can cause inadequate cooling of the condenser coils and compressor. This lack of proper cooling can lead to the compressor overheating. If you are in need of a new refrigerator fan motor you can browse our list of genuine OEM replacement parts to find the right one for your model.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Fridge Fan Motor to Fix a Hot Compressor
sections.text:
1. Locate the fan motor in a cabinet at the bottom of the fridge, near the compressor and condenser coils.
2. Visually inspect the fan motor for any signs of damage, such as burnt wires, excessive dirt or debris buildup, or unusual noise when running. If the fan motor appears damaged or is not running properly, it may need to be replaced.
3. Remove the fan cover to access the motor.
4. Once you have access to the fan motor, carefully disconnect the wires connected to it. Take note of where each wire is connected or take a picture for reference later.
5. Unscrew the fan motor from its mounting bracket or housing.
6. Position the new fan motor in place and secure it with the screws. Make sure it's properly aligned and seated in the mounting bracket.
7. Reconnect the wires to the corresponding terminals on the new fan motor. Double-check that each wire is securely connected and in the correct position.
8. If you removed a back panel to access the fan motor, carefully reattach the panel to the refrigerator. Secure any screws or clips to ensure it's firmly in place.
9. Plug the refrigerator back into the power outlet and turn it on.

sections.heading: How an Overloaded Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
sections.text: When a refrigerator is overcrowded or items are haphazardly placed, it can cause uneven cooling within the compartments, resulting in the compressor running for longer. Additionally, when items are closely packed in together or poorly arranged, it can hinder the airflow through the appliances. The compressor also has to work harder to cool a larger number of items. This forces the refrigerator to work harder to distribute cool air, putting additional strain on the compressor.

sections.heading: How to Store Food Items to Prevent Overheating Compressor
sections.text:
• Keep Air Vents Clear: Make sure that air vents inside the refrigerator are not blocked by food items. This allows for proper airflow and efficient cooling.
• Avoid Overloading: Do not overload the refrigerator with too many items. Leave space between items so that cool air can circulate freely.
• Group Similar Items Together: Organize similar items together to minimize the time the refrigerator door is open. This can help to reduce the amount of warm air that enters the refrigerator and reduces the loss of cool air.
• Regularly Clean and Declutter: Regularly remove old, expired or unused items to maintain an organized and efficient refrigerator.

sections.heading: How Low Voltage Supply to a Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
sections.text: When the compressor motor receives low voltage, it operates at a lower speed than it is designed for. This reduced speed can lead to decreased efficiency, causing the compressor to work harder to maintain the desired cooling temperature. As a result, the compressor generates more heat. Low voltage can also lead to the overloading of various components within the compressor, such as the motor windings and electrical connections, which also results in increased heat production. Over time, the excessive heat buildup can lead to overheating of the compressor.

sections.heading: How to Check for Loose Wiring Near Refrigerator Compressor
sections.text:
1. Unplug the refrigerator from the power outlet before you begin any inspection.
2. The compressor is a large cylindrical component found at the back of the refrigerator, near the bottom. Remove the back panel or grille by unscrewing any screws holding it in place.
3. Look for any visible signs of damage or loose connections in the wiring attached to the compressor.
4. Gently tug on the wires to ensure they are securely connected to the compressor terminals.
5. Check for any burnt or frayed wires, which could indicate a problem.
6. Check the relay and overload protector which are the two components attached to the compressor.
7. Remove these components carefully to inspect the wiring underneath. Ensure the connections are tight and there are no signs of corrosion or damage.
8. Once you have inspected and ensured all connections are secure, reattach the relay and overload protector.
9. Reattach the back panel or grille, and secure it with the screws.
10. Plug the refrigerator back into the power outlet.

sections.heading: How a Poorly Positioned Refrigerator Leads to a Hot Compressor
sections.text:
If the refrigerator is too close to the wall, airflow around the condenser coils will become restricted. As a result, the condenser coils cannot effectively release heat, causing the compressor to work harder to maintain the desired temperature inside the fridge. Furthermore, as the compressor struggles to maintain the desired temperature due to the heat buildup, the refrigerator's cooling performance may be compromised. The food items inside the fridge may not be cooled adequately, and the fridge may run longer and more frequently to achieve the set temperature, resulting in higher energy consumption.
To prevent a hot compressor caused by a fridge being too close to the wall, ensure there is sufficient space around the refrigerator for proper airflow. Pull the fridge forward and leave at least a few inches of clearance between the back of the fridge and the wall, as well as between the sides of the fridge and any nearby objects.

sections.heading: How Low Refrigerant Levels Lead to a Hot Compressor
sections.text:
Refrigerant is responsible for cooling various components of the fridge, including the compressor, condenser, expansion valve, and evaporator to facilitate the cooling process. It absorbs heat from the inside of the refrigerator and releases it outside. When the system lacks sufficient refrigerant, the fridge will be unable to function optimally, leading to overheating and reduced cooling efficiency. Some refrigerants are toxic when inhaled and exposure to high concentrations of these refrigerants can cause dizziness, nausea, and respiratory issues. Refrigerants are also highly flammable and therefore pose a serious fire hazard. It is recommended to avoid addressing this issue on your own and to consult a qualified technician who can check the refrigerant levels and refill them if required.
Understanding why your fridge compressor may be overheating is crucial for maintaining the efficiency and longevity of your refrigerator. By regularly inspecting and addressing these issues, you can prevent compressor overheating and extend the lifespan of your refrigerator. Simple maintenance tasks like cleaning condenser coils, ensuring proper ventilation around the fridge, and checking refrigerant levels can help alleviate the problem. Remember, a well-maintained compressor leads to a cooler, more efficient fridge, ultimately saving you both energy and money in the long run.

title: Why Your Dishwasher is Stopping Mid-Cycle

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• +
General Problems that Cause a Dishwasher to Stop Mid-Cycle
• +
What Parts You Need to Replace to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
A dishwasher stopping mid-cycle can happen for various reasons, often linked to a specific part or problem that will need to be resolved for it to run properly. Signs of a specific issue may include blinking lights, or starting and then stopping abruptly when filling. It's normal for dishwashers to pause mid-cycle to drain or heat water up, but there's a distinct difference between pausing and shutting off completely. Resetting your dishwasher or manually activating the drain can resolve it stopping mid-cycle, but the underlying cause must still be fixed, which means inspecting and testing a number of parts. Whether it's a simple fix like a clogged drain filter or a more complex issue like a malfunctioning door latch assembly or control board, this article will guide you through the required supplies, and instructions for diagnosing and fixing your dishwasher if it's stopping in the middle of a cycle.

sections.heading: General Problems that Cause a Dishwasher to Stop Mid-Cycle
sections.text: It can be frustrating when your dishwasher stops mid-cycle, but understanding some general problems that can cause it will help you fix it quicker. We'll explore a few common issues, like a clogged filter and drain hose, low water pressure, and power failures, to help you resolve this stopping problem quickly and easily.

sections.heading: Clogged Filter and Drain Hose
sections.text:
A dishwasher's filter and hose, which are parts of the draining system, are used to trap food particles and debris from harming valuable parts like the pump, and remove dirty water from the dishwasher. If either of these parts is clogged, blocked, or damaged, the dishwasher will stop to avoid any overflow or potential damage to your home or its parts. If you see a series of lights or an error code appear when this occurs, note it and refer to your user manual for further information on the issue.
1. Unplug your dishwasher and turn off its water supply.
2. Open the dishwasher door and remove its filter. This may require a screwdriver or pliers to remove.
3. Inspect the inside of the filter and its housing for any clogs caused by gunk or debris, and use a brush or sponge, and warm soapy water to clean the filter. If the filter is damaged, replace it immediately.
4. Once the filter and its housing are cleaned, locate the dishwasher's drain hose underneath the sink, and inspect the drain hose for any clogs or foreign objects lodged inside.
5. Place a large bowl or bucket underneath the drain hose opening and disconnect it from the sink drain. Lift the hose and water should rush into the bucket if there's any left. Then use a drain brush to clean it, or replace it if necessary.
6. Reassemble the drain hose and filter assembly, start a cycle, and monitor it for any more stoppages.

sections.heading: Low Water Pressure
sections.text:
The pressure of the water being supplied to the dishwasher is important, because if it's too weak it will cause extended filling times and poor cleaning performance. This is why many dishwashers feature sensors that can accurately detect issues with it, and will stop your dishwasher mid-cycle if not enough water is being supplied.
1. Locate the water supply valves in your home, and inspect its gauge. The reading should be between 14.5 to 80 psi, and a rating over 116 psi would be too high.
2. If your water supply doesn't have a gauge, shut the valves closed.
3. Unplug your dishwasher.
4. Use a screwdriver to unthread the kick plate at the bottom of your dishwasher, and disconnect one of the fill hoses. Expect some water to spill out.
5. Put the fill hose into a bowl or large bucket and turn the corresponding water supply valve until it's open.
6. If the water strength going into the bowl or bucket is weak, you have an issue with your home's water supply. If the water flow is strong, continue reading this guide.

sections.heading: Power Failure
sections.text: Dishwashers can stop suddenly during a cycle due to power problems, either with your home or the appliance itself. Check your circuit breaker for burn marks, and the dishwasher's power cord for damage like breaks or exposed wires. If necessary, contact an electrician to properly inspect and fix your home's circuit breaker or dishwasher's power cord.

sections.heading: What Parts You Need to Replace to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text: When your dishwasher abruptly stops mid-cycle, it's often due to issues with key parts like the door latch, float switch, heating element and fuse, inlet valves, drain pump, and electronic control board. We'll walk you through how to inspect, test, and replace each of these parts, so you can effectively resolve the mid-cycle stopping problem with your dishwasher.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Door Latch to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
The door latch assembly is the most common culprit for dishwashers that stop mid-cycle because the door switch, handle, and latch mechanisms ensure the safe and proper operation of the dishwasher. When these parts break or stop working properly, they can cause the dishwasher to stop mid-cycle due to safety triggers that interpret the door as being open. Unless there's a specific code or indication otherwise, a bad door latch assembly in some models is indicated by the dishwasher stopping mid-cycle and blinking its lights. If your door latch assembly is broken or not working, you may also notice it's easy to open, and tough to close fully.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. Shut off the water supply to your dishwasher.
2. Use a screwdriver to remove the kickplate at the bottom of your dishwasher.
3. Unthread any screws securing your dishwasher below a countertop if necessary, then pull your dishwasher out and unplug it from its wall outlet.
4. Locate the door catch on the upper portion of the dishwasher tub. If it's damaged, replace it by unthreading it and disconnecting its wire harness, and securing the new one.
5. If the door catch isn't broken, the door switch or latch may be. Start by using a screwdriver to unthread the screws around the dishwasher door's inside perimeter.
6. You should now be able to lift and separate the two halves and grab the door switch inside.
7. Remove the wire harnesses from the door switch. If you notice any damage to the latch, like cracks or pieces chipped off, replace it immediately.
8. Locate the door switch on the assembly, and remove it. Then with a multimeter set to ohms, touch each probe to a terminal on the switch. if you don't hear a beep, the switch does not have continuity and will need replacing.
9. Install the switch into the housing, connect its wire harnesses, and install it within the door assembly.
10. Thread the screws back into the door.
11. Begin to carefully close the door, and monitor your dishwasher to see if the stopping issue is resolved.

sections.heading: How to Clean or Replace a Float Switch to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
The float switch in your dishwasher is a safety device that detects water levels to prevent overflowing. Over time it can get covered in gunk or stuck, and may not be operable and able to accurately sense the level of water, causing the mid-cycle stops. We'll explain how to clean and test your dishwasher's float switch with a multimeter and replace it if needed, to get your dishwasher working again, without stoppages.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
• Brush or Sponge
• Drain Brush
• Soap and Warm Water
• Towels
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. First, shut off the water supply to your dishwasher.
2. Use a screwdriver to unthread and remove the kickplate at the bottom of your dishwasher.
3. Disconnect the fill hose from the inlet valve. This may require pliers and towels.
4. Unthread any securing screws holding your dishwasher under your counter, pull it out, and unplug your dishwasher from the wall outlet.
5. Open the dishwasher door and remove the lower dish rack, and locate the top of the float switch.
6. The switch may only be stuck, which can be fixed by moving it up and down. If it's not stuck or if you'd like to test it, remove the stem of the float switch (looks like a mushroom-top), then use a wrench to loosen any securing nuts.
7. Tilt the dishwasher onto its back, so you can access underneath it.
8. Locate the float switch housing and remove the wire harnesses connected to the float switch to remove it.
9. If your float switch is covered in food debris or grime, clean it off with a towel and reinstall it to see if the stopping issue is resolved. Or follow the next steps to test it for continuity.
10. With a multimeter set to continuity, depress the switch and touch the two probes to the terminals on the switch. If you hear a beep, the switch is good. Release the switch and test it again; if there's a beep, the switch is bad and will need replacing.
11. Install the switch back into its housing and connect its wire harnesses.
12. Tilt the dishwasher back and reinstall the stem of the switch.
13. Replace the dish rack and resecure your dishwasher underneath your counter, connect the fill hose, and plug the dishwasher back in.
14. Turn the water supply back on before running a test cycle and seeing if that resolves your issue.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Heating Element to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
Heating elements raise the water temperature for effective dish cleaning and drying, but when a heating element fails, it may also lead to a blown fuse, disrupting the power supply and causing the dishwasher to stop abruptly. We'll help you diagnose and potentially replace a faulty heating element and blown fuse, to fix your dishwasher's mid-cycle stopping.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. Open your dishwasher door and visually inspect the heating element at the bottom of the dishwasher. If it has visible damage, like burns or breaks, it will need to be replaced.
2. Shut off the water valves to your dishwasher.
3. Unthread and remove the kickplate.
4. Disconnect the fill and drain hoses.
5. Unthread any mounting screws keeping your dishwasher under your counter. Then pull it out, and unplug it from the wall outlet.
6. Tilt the dishwasher on its back just enough so you can access the heating element and fuse. The element will likely be at the rear and the fuse at the front.
7. Unplug the wire harnesses connected to the heating element and fuse, then remove them carefully.
8. Test the heating element using a multimeter in continuity mode, by touching each terminal with a probe. If there's no continuity in the heating element or fuse, replace one or both.
9. Install the heating element and fuse back into their respective housings in the dishwasher, and connect their wire harnesses.
10. Tilt the dishwasher back, slide it back into place, plug it in, and thread its mounting screws.
11. Connect its fill and drain hoses, and turn the water valves back on.
12. Start a cycle and monitor your dishwasher to see if the issue returns.

sections.heading: How to Replace an Inlet Valve to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
The inlet valves electronically control the flow of water into your dishwasher during each cycle. When these valves fail, the dishwasher may not receive enough water, resulting in mid-cycle stops. If your dishwasher's inlet valves fail, you might notice water leaking from the bottom while it's running. We'll walk you through a step-by-step process to inspect, troubleshoot, and potentially replace the inlet valves, to get your dishwasher working without interruption.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
• Towels
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. Shut off the water supply to your dishwasher.
2. Unplug your dishwasher from the wall outlet. If that's not possible, turn off the outlet at the breaker.
3. Unthread and remove the dishwasher's kick plate.
4. Locate the inlet valve underneath the dishwasher; it will normally appear as a blue, white, or clear plastic pipe with a wire and bracket attachment.
5. Remove the wires from it, then place towels down before you disconnect the fill hose as well.
6. Inspect the inlet valves, and if no damage is present, use a multimeter to test its continuity.
7. With the multimeter in continuity mode, touch each probe to a terminal on the inlet valve. If the reading is between 500 to 1500 ohms, the valve has continuity. However, if there's no reading, it's weak, or if they're damaged, replace the inlet valves.
8. Install the inlet valve by securing it within the dishwasher bracket and installing its wires and fill hose.
9. Reinstall the kick plate and connect your dishwasher back to power.
10. Begin a cycle and monitor your dishwasher to see if it stops mid-cycle again.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Pump to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
A clogged or malfunctioning dishwasher pump, whether due to mechanical or electrical failure, can cause your dishwasher to stop suddenly during a cycle. However, severe clogs caused by gunk or foreign objects can also lead to this issue. If your dishwasher's pump is clogged, a common sign you may notice is water left at the bottom after a cycle. If this is the case, cleaning or replacing the pump is necessary to get your dishwasher washing properly again.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
• Bucket or Large Bowl
• Brush or Sponge
• Drain Brush
• Soap and Warm Water
• Towels
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. Shut off the dishwasher's water supply.
2. Turn off the dishwasher's power by unplugging it or turning off its breaker.
3. Unthread the dishwasher's kick plate and remove it.
4. Unthread the fill hose from the inlet valve, and disconnect the drain hose from your sink or garbage disposal.
5. Unthread the dishwasher mounting screws under the countertop.
6. Carefully pull the dishwasher out and tilt it on its back to access the pumps.
7. Locate the pump under your dishwasher, and disconnect any wire connectors or hoses connected to it. Your dishwasher may have multiple pumps, which should all be inspected and cleaned, if necessary.
8. Remove the pump and inspect it for any clogs by gunk or foreign objects.
9. If it's not clogged, use a multimeter set to continuity mode, to test the pump for continuity. The pump's terminals should give a reading between 15-40 ohms, and if they give a weak reading, the pump has failed and will need to be replaced.
10. Install the pump, and the necessary wire connectors and hoses.
11. Push the dishwasher back into place, then thread the fill hose to the inlet valve, and install the drain hose underneath your sink.
12. Replace the kick plate, plug in your dishwasher, and turn the water supply on. Run a cycle and see if the dishwasher stops mid-cycle.

sections.heading: How to Replace an Electronic Control Board to Fix a Dishwasher That Stops Mid-Cycle
sections.text:
As the brains of your dishwasher, the electronic control board oversees its various functions. As a result, a malfunctioning control board could be to blame for mid-cycle shutdowns or other system issues, like a short causing it to be unable to properly regulate functions like filling and draining. When this happens, it's important to replace your dishwasher's electronic control board, so it can resume smooth dishwashing without interruption.
Supplies You'll Need
• Philips-head and Flat-head Screwdriver
• Socket Wrench
• Needle-Nose Pliers
• Multimeter
Step-by-Step Guide:
1. Make sure the circuit breaker and water supply to your dishwasher are turned off.
2. Check your owner's manual for the exact location of the electronic control board. Some may be located underneath the appliance, behind the kick plate, whereas others may be located within the door panel, near the control panel.
3. If your model's control board is below the appliance, use a screwdriver to unthread and remove the kickplate to access it. If yours is in the door, unthread the screws around the perimeter of the door's inside frame and separate the two halves.
4. Once you have access to the control board, take note of the wire connectors attached to the control board, and disconnect them.
5. Take the new electronic control board and plug in the necessary wire connectors to install it.
6. Reassemble your dishwasher door or kick plate, turn the circuit breaker back on, and run a test cycle to ensure the dishwasher works again.
Now that your dishwasher is running again without interruption, you can get back to the convenience of clean dishes without having to hand-wash them! Two Methods to Reset Your Frigidaire Fridge
Is your Frigidaire fridge acting up, leaving you with lukewarm drinks and thawing food? Resetting your Frigidaire refrigerator can often work wonders, and help you tackle issues from temperature problems to control panel glitches. In this article, we'll show how to perform a soft reset and a hard reset of your Frigidaire fridge and help you understand when and why it might be necessary, such as after a power surge or when the fridge is displaying an error code. Whether you're facing a minor glitch or major malfunctions, a reset could be just the ticket to restore your appliance's cool confidence.

sections.heading: When to Reset Your Frigidaire Fridge
sections.text:
• After a Power Surge: Power outages or electrical surges can sometimes disrupt the normal functioning of electronic appliances like refrigerators. Resetting the fridge can help restore it to normal operation after such events.
• Error Code Displayed: If your fridge displays error codes indicating a malfunction, resetting it can clear these codes and potentially resolve the underlying issue.
• Temperature Issues: If your fridge is not cooling or freezing properly, resetting it can help recalibrate the temperature settings and resolve the issue.
• Control Panel Malfunction: Sometimes, the control panel on your fridge may freeze or malfunction, causing it to stop responding to commands. Resetting the fridge can often fix this problem.

sections.heading: Two Methods to Reset Your Frigidaire Fridge
1. Use the Reset Button or Crush Button on Your Frigidaire Fridge
sections.text: First, check if your fridge has a Reset button on the control panel at the front of the fridge. Once you have located it, press and hold the button for 5 seconds. If there is no Reset button, press and hold the Crush button for 5 seconds instead. You may see lights flashing on the control panel flash or hear a beeping as the fridge returns to its default settings. Once the reset process is complete, monitor how your refrigerator is performing over the next few hours to ensure that it is functioning properly again.

sections.heading: 2. Turn Off the Circuit Breaker for Your Frigidaire Fridge
sections.text:
If using the Reset button or Crush button does not reset the refrigerator, you can perform a hard reset instead. Locate the circuit breaker in your home and look for the switch that corresponds to the refrigerator. Flip the switch to the off position and wait at least 5 minutes to allow the refrigerator to completely power down. Turn the switch back on and allow the fridge to recalibrate itself. You should hear the compressor and fans running, which indicates that power has been restored. Once the fridge is fully powered up you can check to see if it's functioning properly and if there are no longer any error codes or control panel issues.
Knowing when and how to reset your Frigidaire fridge can be a valuable skill for maintaining its optimal performance and extending its lifespan. Whether you're experiencing temperature fluctuations, malfunctioning displays, or other issues, a reset can often provide a simple solution. By following the steps outlined in this guide and understanding the common reasons why a reset may be necessary, you can ensure that your Frigidaire refrigerator continues to keep your food fresh and your kitchen running smoothly. However, if resetting does not resolve the issue, then your fridge may need repair. You can use our model search feature to find genuine OEM Frigidaire refrigerator parts for your appliance. With proper care and maintenance, your Frigidaire fridge will continue to serve you well for years to come.

sections.heading: Introduction

How to Use the Power Cool Feature on Your Samsung Fridge

• +
What to Do When Power Cool in Your Samsung Fridge is Not Working

Whether you're restocking groceries or preparing for gatherings, Power Cool is a feature available on many Samsung refrigerators, designed to rapidly lower the temperature inside the fridge compartment. Power Cool is commonly used after grocery shopping, when preparing for gatherings, or during hot weather conditions. To activate Power Cool, you can use either the control panel on the refrigerator or the Family Hub app. Factors influencing the duration of Power Cool include initial temperature, amount and temperature of contents, room temperature, refrigerator age, frequency of door openings, and the size and model of the refrigerator. If Power Cool is not working, you can try resetting the refrigerator to restore it to its original settings. Ultimately, Samsung's Power Cool feature offers a convenient way to ensure your food stays cool and your groceries remain fresh for longer. Follow this guide to learn how to get the most out of this feature!

sections.heading: What is Power Cool on a Samsung Refrigerator?
sections.text: Power Cool allows you to lower the temperature inside the refrigerator compartment quickly. When Power Cool is activated, the refrigerator begins to run the compressor at a higher capacity to help cool down the interior rapidly. This feature allows you to instantly chill the food items stored in the fridge compartment.

sections.heading: What is Power Freeze on a Samsung Refrigerator?
sections.text: The Power Freeze feature works similarly to the Power Cool feature by running the compressor at a higher capacity, but it is used for the freezer compartment. It is designed to rapidly freeze items and is usually activated when you need to quickly freeze fresh groceries or items such as ice cream. The Power Freeze function also shortens the amount of time needed to produce ice from the ice maker. It is best to activate Power Freeze one full day before you place items in the freezer. Once it is activated, Power Freeze will run for 50 hours before gradually returning to the normal freezer temperature. To activate and deactivate it, simply press and hold the Freezer button for 3 seconds or select the Power Freeze option in your Family Hub account.

sections.heading: How Long Does Power Cool Stay On?
sections.text: It generally takes approximately two hours for the fridge to fully cool after Power Cool is activated. Once the temperature reaches 1°C the Power Cool function switches off. After several hours the fridge will gradually return to its normal temperature.

sections.heading: When to use Power Cool on a Samsung Refrigerator?
sections.text:
Power Cool is a powerful and convenient way to cool the interior of the fridge. You can use Power Cool in the following scenarios to help get the most out of your appliance:
• After Grocery Shopping: You can use Power Cool to quickly chill newly purchased perishables, ensuring they remain fresh for longer periods. This is great for items such as fruits and vegetables which tend to go bad faster than other food items.
• Preparing for Gatherings: When you are expecting guests or hosting a party, you can activate Power Cool to rapidly chill beverages. This allows you and your guests to enjoy refreshments without any delay.
• Emergency Thawing: In the event of unexpected thawing or partially melted frozen items, such as due to a power outage or a fault in the fridge, you can activate the Power Cool to quickly restore the optimal temperature inside the fridge and preserve food quality. This means you can save money and avoid throwing out your food.
• Hot Weather Conditions: During the hot summer months, the Power Cool feature is a great way to combat temperature fluctuations and maintain consistent cooling performance in order to protect your food from spoiling.
• Post-Cooking: After cooking a large meal, you can use Power Cool to quickly cool down leftovers before storing them in the refrigerator, preventing bacterial growth and maintaining food safety. Note that you should avoid placing very hot items in the fridge as hot items will release steam which condenses on the shelves and walls of the fridge. This creates a humid environment which can promote bacterial growth and increase food spoilage.
• Refrigerator Overload: When the refrigerator is overloaded with items, enabling Power Cool allows cold air to circulate through the fridge faster which ensures efficient cooling throughout the appliance. However, it is important to note that the fridge will need to use significant energy to run Power Cool when it is overloaded.

sections.heading: How to Use the Power Cool Feature on Your Samsung Fridge
1. Use the Samsung Fridge Button
sections.text: Locate the "Fridge" button on the control panel of your refrigerator. Press and hold the button for 3 seconds and wait for the corresponding display to light up. This indicates that Power Cool is now running You can switch off the Power Cool function by pressing and holding the button again until the indicator light switches off.

sections.heading: 2. Use the Samsung Family Hub App
sections.text: First ensure that your Samsung refrigerator is connected to your home Wi-Fi network and that you have the SmartThings App installed on your phone or tablet. Log in to your account and connect the refrigerator to your Family Hub account. Navigate to the Fridge Manager button and click on it. Tap on the toggle labeled Power Cool to activate Power Cool in your fridge. Once Power Cool has been activated, you can monitor the temperature inside the refrigerator from your phone. You may also receive notifications or updates through the Family Hub app.

sections.heading: Factors that Affect Duration of Power Cool
sections.text:
The duration of the Power Cool feature can be influenced by several factors:
• Initial Temperature: The starting temperature inside the refrigerator affects how long the Power Cool feature will need to run to reach 1°C. If the fridge is already low, Power Cool might not need to run for as long.
• Amount and Temperature of Contents: The more and warmer the items you've just placed in the fridge, the longer Power Cool may need to run to bring the overall temperature down. If you've just done a large grocery shopping trip and filled the fridge with items then, Power Cool will need more time to chill all the items.
• Average Room Temperature: The temperature of the kitchen can impact how quickly the fridge can cool down. If the room temperature is warmer, the fridge will have to work harder to cool down. This is especially true in the summer months when average temperatures are higher.
• Refrigerator Age: As the refrigerator ages, parts such as the compressor, condenser coils, and seals may wear down, leading to reduced cooling efficiency and increased energy consumption. In such cases, the Power Cool feature will still work as intended, but it might take longer to achieve the desired temperature or require more energy to operate. If you have noticed that your fridge is not running efficiently, it may be due for some maintenance.
• Frequency of Door Openings: Opening the refrigerator door frequently during the Power Cool cycle allows warm air to enter the fridge compartment which can increase the amount of the refrigerator needs to cool down.
• Size of the Refrigerator: Larger refrigerators with more internal volume may require longer Power Cool cycles to reach the desired temperature compared to smaller models.

sections.heading: What to Do When Power Cool in Your Samsung Fridge is Not Working
sections.text: If the Power Cool feature is not working, it may be due to a minor system glitch in the refrigerator. It is common for users to run into technical problems every so often. You can fix this issue by resetting the refrigerator. This will clear out any old settings and restore the fridge to its default settings. You can follow any of the methods below to rest your Samsung fridge.

sections.heading: 1. Press the Reset Button on Your Samsung Fridge
sections.text: Locate the Reset button on the control panel on the refrigerator. Once you have found it, press and hold the button for 3 - 5 seconds. The control panel should light up as it resets. Once the display has returned to normal check that the fridge is running properly again.

sections.heading: 2.Press the Power Cool and Power Freeze buttons on Your Samsung Fridge
sections.text: If your Samsung fridge does not have a Reset button, you can use the Power Cool and Power Freeze buttons to reset the fridge instead. Press and hold the buttons together, at the same time for 10 seconds. You should hear a chime as the refrigerator resets itself.

sections.heading: 3. Use the Family Hub App to Reset Your Samsung Fridge
sections.text: Open the Family Hub App on your phone and click on the Settings button. Scroll down to the option that says "About Family Hub". Select the "Factory data reset" option and then press on the "RESET" option. The app will then prompt you to press "RESET" again. Finally, press "Delete all data".

sections.heading: 4. Turn Off the Circuit Breaker for your Samsung Fridge
sections.text: Go to the electrical panel in your home and find the switch that corresponds to the refrigerator. Flip the switch and leave it turned off for at least five minutes. This allows the electronic controls and components to reset completely. Turn the switch back on and allow the fridge to power on and stabilize. Verify that the refrigerator is functioning properly again after the hard reset.

sections.heading: What to Do if Power Freeze Keeps Turning On By Itself
sections.text:
A common problem that Samsung fridge users face is the Power Freeze function cycling on on its own. This typically indicates a stuck key or an internal fault within the display panel on the front of the refrigerator. You can browse our list of genuine OEM Samsung refrigerator parts to find a replacement for your model! To remove the display panel, first locate and unthread the mounting screws(s) located on the underside of the panel. Once you have done so you can grip the bottom of the panel with both hands and pull it out of the housing. Disconnect the wire connector and discard the old panel. Attach the wire connector to your new display panel and pop it back into the housing. Remember to rethread the mounting screw to hold it in place.
Samsung's Power Cool feature is a powerful tool designed to rapidly cool down your refrigerator's interior, ensuring your groceries stay fresh for longer. By activating this feature strategically during periods of high usage or after loading in a large batch of warm items, you can maintain optimal temperature levels and preserve the quality of your stored food. Remember that while Power Cool is incredibly effective, using it excessively can lead to unnecessary energy consumption. So be sure to follow the guidelines set out above on when and how to use the Power Cool feature for maximum efficiency.

How to Turn On and Turn Off an LG Washer Control Lock
• How to Reset an LG Washer to Turn Off a Control Lock
If your LG washer is flashing a ‘CL’ code, it signifies that the 'control lock', also known as the ‘child lock’, is turned on. This ‘CL’ code is not an error, but a notification that the control lock is active, causing the control panel buttons and dial, except the power button, to be unresponsive to inputs or changes. The control lock is important because it prevents accidental washer use, especially by children. In this article, we'll explain how to activate and deactivate this lock for front and top-load washers and provide steps on how to reset your LG washer if you have difficulties deactivating the ‘CL’ code.
It is worth noting that LG washers, dryers, and dishwashers share the ‘CL’ code between them. This means the process of turning the control lock on or off works the same way, and the following guide can be used to resolve any issues with any of them. If you need to reset your LG washer, dryer, or dishwasher, you can also use the same set of instructions to do so.

sections.heading: How to Turn On and Turn Off an LG Washer Control Lock
sections.text: There is no difference in the activation process for top-load and front-load LG washers, but instead, it depends on whether you have a single or double-button control lock model. In either case, we'll explain how to activate and deactivate the control lock, so you can get back to washing your clothes.

sections.heading: Turn On and Turn Off an LG Washer Control Lock with a Single Button
sections.text:
If you own an LG washer with a single, designated control lock button, the activation and deactivation process is quite straightforward. If you're unsure whether your model is a single or double-button model, use your owner's manual to identify which you have.
1. To activate the control lock, locate the designated control lock button, and hold it for 3–5 seconds to turn it on.
2. A chime should sound, and a 'CL' code will begin to flash on the display, as well as the remaining cycle time if a cycle was started. On some LG washer models, a small lock icon with a smiley face will appear. Note: If you turn the lock on during a wash cycle and fail to deactivate it before the cycle completes, the lock will remain on even after the washer turns off.
3. To turn off the control lock for your LG washer, hold the same button for 3–5 seconds. Another chime should sound, and the 'CL' code will disappear from the display.

sections.heading: Turn On and Turn Off an LG Washer Control Lock with Two Buttons
sections.text:
If your LG washer has two ‘Control Lock’ labelled buttons side-by-side instead of one, use those to turn the lock on or off. If the buttons aren't labelled, or you're unsure which buttons to press, use your owner's manual to help you identify which buttons you need to use.
1. To activate the control lock on your washer, identify which two buttons are used to activate it.
2. Hold the two buttons you've identified for 3–5 seconds to activate and turn on the control lock. A chime should sound, and a 'CL' code should appear and begin flashing. For some models, a small lock icon with a smiley face will appear until the lock is turned off. Note: If you activate the lock during a wash cycle and you do not turn it off before the cycle ends, the lock will remain on even after it ends and the washer turns off.
3. To turn off the control lock, hold the same buttons used to turn on the lock for 3–5 seconds. A chime should sound, and the 'CL' code and any lock symbols will disappear.

sections.heading: How to Reset an LG Washer to Turn Off a Control Lock
sections.text:
You may encounter an issue where the control lock will not deactivate from your LG washer, even after you hold down the necessary button(s) for 3–5 seconds. If this happens, you will need to perform a reset of your LG washer, which we will explain exactly how to do.
1. Perform a hard reset of your washer by unplugging its power cord from the wall outlet or turning off its breaker.
2. After 5 minutes the washer should be fully reset, and you can reconnect its breaker or plug it back into the wall outlet. At this point, the 'CL' code should no longer appear, and you should be able to use the washer fully again.
Now that you know how to activate and deactivate your LG washer's control lock, you can not only prevent any children from accessing your washer while it's on, but you can be rest assured that your washer fully works again! Top 3 Methods to Reset Your GE Profile Refrigerator Ice Maker

If your GE Profile refrigerator ice maker is having difficulties producing or dispensing ice, a quick reset of the ice maker can often resolve these issues. It is best to reset your ice maker if it is newly installed, after a power outage, or when it is experiencing system errors. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps to reset your GE Profile refrigerator's ice maker, ensuring you can enjoy a steady supply of ice for your beverages. If the ice maker is still not working after a reset, you will need to inspect it further for possible faulty parts, water supply issues, or excessive ice build-up.

sections.heading: When to Reset Your GE Profile Refrigerator Ice Maker
sections.text:
• Difficulties Making or Dispensing Ice: If your ice maker suddenly stops producing ice or if there is a noticeable decrease in the amount of ice produced, resetting can often resolve the issue by clearing out any minor glitches.
• Power Surge or Outage: Power interruptions can disrupt the normal operation of the refrigerator and ice maker. When the power is out, the appliance loses any stored settings or programming. Therefore, a reset is a useful way to restore its settings and resume normal operation as well as to synchronize the ice maker with other parts of the refrigerator and ensure they work well together.
• Malfunctioning Sensor: The ice maker temperature sensor helps to determine when to start the ice-making cycle. If it is experiencing an error, which can be caused by a power outage or other system failure, the ice maker may not produce any ice. Resetting the appliance can help to clear this error.
• System Error: A system error is typically caused by a malfunction or fault within the electronic control system. This error can show up in various ways, such as the ice maker not producing ice, producing ice of poor quality, or displaying error codes or warning lights on the control panel. The error code most commonly associated with ice maker problems is the CI error code.

sections.heading: Top 3 Methods to Reset Your GE Profile Refrigerator Ice Maker
sections.text: Determining the right method to reset your fridge ice maker depends on the specific model of your GE Profile refrigerator. However, each of the following three methods is an effective way to reset your GE Profile ice maker. You can begin with the first method and proceed to the next, if necessary, until you find the one that works best for your ice maker.

sections.heading: Press and Hold the Reset Button
sections.text:
1. Locate the reset button on the control panel of the refrigerator.
2. Press and hold the button for 3- 5 seconds.
3. Allow the ice maker to cycle through before attempting to dispense any ice.

sections.heading: Turn the GE Ice Maker Switch Off
sections.text:
1. Open the refrigerator to access the ice maker unit.
2. Locate the shut-off switch on the front of the unit and turn the switch off.
3. Wait several 15-30 seconds before turning the switch back on.

sections.heading: Push the GE Ice Maker Paddle 3 times.
sections.text:
1. Locate the shut-off switch for the ice maker and turn it off.
2. You may need to remove the ice maker tray for better access to the ice maker paddle, also known as the feeler arm or bail arm.
3. Wait 30 seconds to 1 minute and then turn the switch back on.
4. Immediately push the ice maker paddle upwards 3 times.
5. Let the ice maker cycle through before resuming use.

sections.heading: Common Causes of GE Profile Refrigerator Ice Maker Failure
sections.text:
If resetting the ice maker doesn't resolve the issue, there may be a more serious issue causing the malfunction. You can use our ice maker troubleshooting guide to help you fix your GE Profile ice maker. The most common causes of ice maker malfunctions include the following:
• Stuck Bail Arm: The bail arm detects the amount of ice in the ice bin. Once the bin is full, the arm is pushed upwards to turn off the ice maker. The arm may become stuck in this position. If the bail arm is stuck in the engaged position the ice maker will think that the bin is full and will fail to produce any ice.
• Water Supply Issues: Problems with the water supply line, such as low water pressure, a clogged filter, or a frozen water line, can inhibit the ice maker's ability to produce ice. Resetting the ice maker won't address these issues, which may require troubleshooting and repairs to the water supply system.
• Ice Jam: If there is an excessive build-up of ice in the ice bucket, the ice maker will be unable to produce or dispense more ice. Furthermore, if ice cubes get stuck between moving parts it can hinder the ice maker's ability to cycle and produce new ice and potentially damage the unit. You will need to first clear away all the built-up ice to fix the ice maker.
• Mechanical Issues: The ice maker's motor, gears, or ejector blades, may be worn out, damaged, or misaligned, preventing the ice maker from operating correctly even after a reset. Additionally, damage to the ice maker's parts, such as a cracked housing or a broken seal, may prevent it from functioning properly. Resetting the ice maker won't repair physical damage. You will need to replace the faulty parts.
• Electrical Problems: Faulty electrical connections, wiring issues, or a malfunctioning control board can also prevent the ice maker from functioning properly.
• Sensor Malfunctions: If the ice maker relies on sensors to detect ice levels or monitor temperature, a malfunctioning sensor can prevent it from operating correctly. Resetting the ice maker may not fix sensor-related issues, which may require calibration or replacement of the sensor.
Resetting your GE Profile ice maker can be a simple yet effective solution to many common issues that may arise, such as sudden difficulties in ice production or malfunctioning sensors. By following the steps outlined in this guide, you can restore your ice maker to proper functioning. If you require new parts to get your ice maker up and running again, you can browse our list of genuine OEM GE Profile ice maker parts. With proper maintenance and occasional troubleshooting, you can keep your GE Profile ice maker running smoothly and enjoy its convenience for years to come.

How to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
If your Whirlpool washer won’t lock, it’s likely due to malfunctioning locking safety devices. Front and top-load washer models differ in locking systems, and the parts you will need to fix will differ as well. Top-load washers won’t lock because of issues with their lid, lid switch and actuator, lid lock, or control board. Whereas front-load models may have problems with the door latch/strike, door seal, door hinge, or control board. We’ll guide you step-by-step to resolve this issue and get your washer locking and working again.

sections.heading: Why is Your Whirlpool Washer Not Locking?
sections.text: If your Whirlpool washer isn't locking properly, there may be a few reasons why. If any of the parts in your washer's locking mechanism are broken or worn out, it can cause the whole lock to not line up correctly or work at all. Below we will explain why your washer needs to lock in the first place, the signs your washer has a locking issue, and the distinct differences between top-load and front-load Whirlpool washer lock parts.

sections.heading: Why Your Washer Needs to Lock
sections.text: The entire reason your washer needs to lock is for safety reasons. The inner tub of your washer, whether it's a top-load or front-load model will, at some point during the washing cycle, begin to spin at RPM's (rotations per minute) that can be hazardous if insecure. Your washer is equipped with a locking mechanism to ensure you can't have any contact with it during these points. Some models outright lock the washer until the cycle is over, whereas some models will allow you to pause or stop the cycle to throw another garment in. But the lock is there as a preventative measure to ensure you or any children don't get injured.

sections.heading: Signs That Your Whirlpool Washer has a Locking Issue
sections.text:
If you're unsure of what's going on with your Whirlpool washer, and you're curious if what you're seeing or hearing is a locking issue, these are the following signs.
• Clicking Noises: If you hear a repeated clicking noise when starting a washing cycle with your Whirlpool washer, that is the sound of the lock attempting to connect and being unable to do so. Avoid hitting your washer to fix this, as you may cause more damage to it.
• Flashing Lock Light: Seeing a blinking or flashing 'lock' light on your Whirlpool washer is a sign that there is an issue with the locking system as a whole. The user manual for some models may indicate particular parts or give an error code with a specific issue. Make sure to reference your manual for those codes.
• Washer Not Starting: Another common sign is that your washer simply won't start. As mentioned earlier, your washer will not start if it cannot lock securely.

sections.heading: Differences Between Top-Load and Front-Load Washer Locks
sections.text:
Since front-load and top-load Whirlpool washers have distinctly different structures, they also feature different parts in their locking mechanisms. There may also be differences in older versus newer models, so be sure to check your specific model and its user manual for any indication of what lock yours has.
Top-Load Washer Lock Parts
• Lid
• Lid Switch and Actuator
• Lid Lock
• Control Board
Front-Load Washer Lock Parts
• Door Latch/Strike
• Door Switch
• Door Seal (also known as a Boot) and Retaining Ring
• Door Hinge
• Control Board

sections.heading: How to Fix a Top-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text: Now that you know why your Whirlpool washer needs to lock, the signs that your washer has a locking issue, and all of the parts that can cause this issue, you can fix it! With a top-load Whirlpool washer, all of the affected parts that can malfunction and cause a lock-related issue are located at the top and rear of the washer, and will need minimal tools (screwdriver, wrench, and pliers) to access and replace!

sections.heading: How to Replace a Lid Switch to Fix a Top-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
The lid switch and actuator for a top-load Whirlpool washer are responsible for communicating that the lid is closed, with the control board. If either are broken or malfunctioning, the control board will not start or lock properly as a result. Removing a lid switch to test and/or replace is easy, and with our instructions you will have no issue getting your washer running again. To do this repair, you will need a multimeter, screwdriver or wrench, and flat tool like a putty knife.
1. Unplug your washer's power cord.
2. Lift the lid of the washer and unthread any mounting screws on the top panel around the entrance of the washer.
3. If you notice any unusual bends or warps in your washer's lid that could cause misalignment between the switch and actuator, replace it immediately.
4. Slide the top panel forward and use a putty knife or flat tool to lift the top panel of your washer.
5. Locate the lid switch on the underside of the top panel, and disconnect its wire harness to effectively remove it. Locate the actuator as well, which is normally on the underside of the lid.
6. Test the old switch to verify that it's not physically damaged. Then test it with a multimeter for continuity by setting it to the Rx1 setting, and touching the probes to the terminals with the switch button down; you should receive a setting of zero.
7. If your switch is physically damaged or not reading 0 when activated, make sure to replace it immediately. If the actuator for the switch is also damaged and unable to fully activate the switch, replace it by unthreading its screws.
8. Plug in the new switch via its wire harness and secure it below the washer's top panel.
9. Close your washer and make sure the actuator fully sits within the switch before you plug the washer back in and attempt to run a cycle.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Lid Lock to Fix a Top-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
Some models of top-load washers feature a lid lock, that is similar in function and appearance to a lid switch, however, its sole purpose is securing the lid during the washing cycle. If the lid lock for your top-load Whirlpool washer is damaged or not locking properly, you will need to replace it immediately. To do this repair, you will need a screwdriver and/or wrench, multimeter and flat tool.
1. Unplug your washer's power cord.
2. Unthread any securing screws holding the top panel down, at the top of your washer's back panel. Depending on your washer, you may also need to remove the back panel to access the control board and its wire harness connections.
3. Slide the top panel forward and use a putty knife or other flat tool to lift the top panel of your washer.
4. Locate the lid lock underneath the top panel, and use a screwdriver to unthread it or release its securing clips. Then, trace its wire harness and disconnect it.
5. Inspect the lock for any damage, and then use a multimeter in the ohms setting (Rx1) and touch each probe to a terminal on the lock; the reading should be infinity. Depress it and the reading should be zero - if not, it needs to be replaced.
6. Install the new (or existing) lid lock and by securing it with the necessary screws or clips, and by plugging in the necessary wire harness to the control board.
7. Secure the top panel of the washer, and secure the back panel of the washer.
8. Plug the washer back in and monitor for any other locking issues.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Control Board to Fix a Top-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
Any issues with a top-load washer, including any issues where the locking mechanism is not working or engaging, can ultimately boil down to the control board not working properly. If this happens, it's important to replace the control board as soon as possible, as you won't be able to use your Whirlpool washer until you do so. Replacing a control board will require a screwdriver and/or wrench, and a set of pliers, if necessary.
1. Unplug your washer's power cord.
2. Locate the control board for your washer. Top-load machines normally feature the control board at the rear of the machine.
3. Use a screwdriver or wrench to unthread the back panel of the washer.
4. With the back panel removed, locate the control board and take note of the wires connected to it.
5. Disconnect the wire harnesses (with a set of pliers, if necessary), and use a screwdriver to unthread the securing screws for the control board.
6. Remove the old control board and install the new one, and then secure it with the necessary screws.
7. Connect the wire harnesses to the new control board and replace the back panel of the washer.
8. Plug your washer back in and monitor it for any further locking issues.

sections.heading: How to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text: Fixing a front-load Whirlpool washer that won't lock is not a difficult task. You will need some tools to inspect and potentially replace parts like the door latch, door switch, door seal and door hinge. But we've got the step-by-step instructions that will explain exactly how to do it, so you can quickly get your front-load washer back in fully working condition.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Door Latch to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
The door latch is an essential part in the washer's ability to properly lock shut. The door latch, also known as a strike, inserts into the door switch and allows the lock to secure the door completely. If the latch is broken, warped or damaged, it can cause enough of a misalignment for the locking mechanism to no longer work; at which point, it would need to be replaced. Replacing a front-load washer's door latch will only require a screwdriver.
1. Open your washer's door and locate the door latch. This will be on the inside of the door, opposite of the door hinge.
2. Inspect the latch for any physical damage. If it's warped, chipped, or broken, and unable to seat properly in the switch, it needs to be replaced.
3. Use a screwdriver to unthread the door latch from the inside of the door.
4. Remove the old door latch, and attach the new one - then secure it with the appropriate screw.
5. Close your door and see if the locking issue is resolved.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Door Switch to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
Door switches, also known as door locks, work with the door latch to hold and secure the door shut during the washing cycle. When a door switch is damaged or bad, either physically or mechanically, it will cause locking issues and the cycle will not start, effectively rendering your washer inoperable. However, we have the instructional guide that you can follow to find out if your washer's door switch is in need of immediate replacement, or if there's another part that should be looked at. Replacing a door switch will require a screwdriver, a set of pliers, and a multimeter.
1. Unplug your washer from the wall outlet.
2. Open your washer's door and locate the door switch, which should be on the door frame and identifiable by its female port.
3. To access the door switch, you will need to trace the door seal and pull the retaining ring and its spring out - this is best done by hand with a set of needle-nose pliers.
4. With the retaining ring out, you can pull the door seal away from the location of the door switch assembly. This will allow you to remove it.
5. Use a screwdriver (or drill) to unthread the door switch assembly from the washer door frame.
6. With the door switch assembly loose, pull back the seal and handle the switch.
7. Disconnect its wire harness and remove it.
8. Use a multimeter in the Rx1 setting to test the switch for continuity while the switch is activated with the latch. Inspect the door switch for any signs of physical damage, and if the switch is damaged and broken, or does not have continuity, it needs to be replaced.
9. Plug the wiring harness into the new switch and secure it being the washer's door frame.
10. Pull the door seal back onto the door frame and ensure it's sealed and flush within its groove.
11. Wrap the retaining ring around the door seal and use needle-nose pliers to pull on its spring to seat it within the groove of the seal. Ensure the ring is seated properly before continuing.
12. Plug the washer back in and run a cycle to see if the locking issue is resolved.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Door Seal to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
Although less common of a problem with a washer door locking than the previously mentioned parts, a door seal can be just as guilty at causing a misalignment for the door lock. Door seals, also known as boots, bellows, or gaskets, are used to ensure the washer door doesn't leak. If the door seal is damaged or warped, it can may cause the door or tub to not shut properly, resulting in the lock not being able to fully close. Replacing a door seal will require a screwdriver and a set of needle-nose pliers or flat-head screwdriver.
1. Unplug your washer from the wall outlet.
2. Open the washer door and locate the seal around the frame of the door.
3. Inspect the seal for any warps, tears, or damage. If it's damaged in any way or not allowing the door to sit properly when closed, replace it.
4. Trace your hand around the seal until you can you feel the metal retaining ring and its spring. Stretch the spring and pull off the ring to remove it. If the retaining ring is warped, bent, or severely stretched, replace it.
5. With the ring out, begin to pull the seal away from the washer door frame. Depending on your model, you may need to use a screwdriver or drill to unthread a securing screw inside the washer.
6. Remove the old seal and insert the new one. Install it by carefully wrapping it around the inner tub of the washer, and then securing it with a screw if necessary for your model. If this is too difficult to do by hand, you may need to remove the front panel of the washer by first removing the top panel, and then carefully disassembling the front assembly.
7. Once the new seal is installed, ensure it's wrapped around the door frame of the washer, and then wrap the retaining ring around it to secure it in place - this may be most easily done with pliers.
8. Once the new seal is installed, close the washer door and see if the locking issue is resolved.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Door Hinge to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
The hinge to any appliance, especially Whirlpool washers, will cause closing, locking, and securing issues if it's bent or damaged in any way. It's important that if your Whirlpool washer's door hinge is bent or damaged, that it be replaced as soon as possible. To replace a front-load Whirlpool washer's door hinge, you will only need a screwdriver or wrench.
1. Open your washer's door and locate the door hinge on the inside portion, opposite the door latch.
2. Use a screwdriver to unthread the screws securing the door hinge.
3. Once the screws are removed, lift the door up to remove it.
4. Place the door on a flat surface, and use a screwdriver to unthread the screws securing the inner and outer door halves together.
5. Separate the two halves, and use a screwdriver to unthread any cover plates on the door hinge.
6. Remove any covers, and remove the old door hinge.
7. Position the hinge on the door and push it in to install it. Make sure any cover plates are installed as well.
8. Replace the two halves of the door together and secure them with the necessary screws.
9. Reseat the door on the washer frame, and secure the hinge with its screws.
10. Close the door and see if the locking issue is resolved.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Control Board to Fix a Front-Load Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Lock
sections.text:
The control board is the central system that runs your Whirlpool washer, and ensures it moves through the washing cycle properly. If your washer's lock is no longer engaging, and you've checked your washer's other parts for damage and functionality, and found none, the main control board is responsible and will need to be replaced. Replacing a front-load washer's control board will require tools like a screwdriver or drill, and a set of pliers (if necessary).
1. Unplug your washer from the wall outlet.
2. Use a screwdriver to unthread the top panel's securing screws on the back of the washer.
3. Remove the top panel.
4. Locate the control board. If it's in the washer's front panel and inaccessible from the top, you will need to remove the door and disconnect the front panel from the washer to gain access to it.
5. Unclip any covers on top of the board, and once you have access to the control board, you should note any wire harness connected to it.
6. Disconnect its wire harnesses, and then unthread and remove the control board.
7. With the old board removed, install the new board into the washer, and secure it with the necessary screws or clips. Install any covers onto the board as well.
8. Reassemble your washer if you had to remove the front panel, and then reseat the top panel of the washer. Make sure to secure it with its screws as well.
9. Plug your washer back in, and your locking issues should be gone!
Now that your Whirlpool washer is locking properly, you're not only able to wash your clothes, but you can fix any of these issues with your washer if they ever pop-up again! And in the spirit of popping up, if any of the other appliances you use have error codes or other issues in the future, or if you're just looking for some fun or helpful DIY guides, hop on over to our other PartSelect blogs!

title: How to Fix a Frigidaire Dishwasher that Won't Drain

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:

How a Clogged Frigidaire Dishwasher Filter Causes Poor Drainage

• +
How a Blocked Frigidaire Dishwasher Drain Pump Causes Poor Drainage
• +

• +
