How to Fix a Leaking GE Dishwasher
• How to Prevent Future Leaks in Your GE Dishwasher
If your GE dishwasher is leaking from the bottom of its door, there is likely a part within your dishwasher that's worn out or damaged, like the door gasket, inlet valve, float switch, hose, or pump. Replacing any of these parts is quite simple, but will require some tools and some DIY time!

sections.heading: Why is my GE Dishwasher Leaking from the Bottom of the Door?
sections.text:
If you notice that your dishwasher has a leak, there are some tell-tale signs to look out for to help you figure out which parts are ultimately causing the leak, which you can then inspect and replace or fix!
• Reduced Cleaning Performance: Any amount of water leaking from your dishwasher can reduce the cleaning ability of the dishwasher as a whole, so if you're noticing a significant drop in dishwasher cleaning performance, like dishes not being cleaned fully, it means there's a part like the filter, inlet valve or drain pump that are causing it.
• Mildew or Mold: Another easy sign of a leak or water presence in general is mold or mildew growth. Normally mold or mildew will also come with an unpleasant smell, so seeing or smelling it is an easy indication of a leak from somewhere underneath your dishwasher, such as the drain pump, hose or inlet valve.
• Unusual Noises: A not-so obvious sign that you may not think of is sound, specifically unusual sounds like gurgling or bubbling can be associated with a clogged drain hose or improperly sealed pump.
• Water Not Draining: If after a load of dishes you notice water still left in the dishwasher, it's a sign that one of the parts within the draining system for the dishwasher is either clogged or not working as it should, which could or potentially may already have resulted in leaks.

sections.heading: How to Fix a Leaking GE Dishwasher
sections.text: Now if you're seeing, hearing, or smelling any of those signs, there is a good chance a part (or multiple of them) are damaged, defective, or broken. Replacing a part in your dishwasher, however, is quite simple and will only require some tools, dedicated DIY time, and step-by-step guides to show you exactly how to fix your dishwasher.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Damaged or Torn Door Gasket in a GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
The easiest part to replace in your dishwasher that could be causing a leak is the door gasket. The gasket for your GE dishwasher is the rubber material that surrounds the door frame that's intended to seal the interior of the dishwasher cabinet from the inside of your home, and if it's torn or damaged will lead to water leaking. This is one of the most common causes of dishwashers leaking, and will result in you finding water at the bottom of the front of your dishwasher, during or after a cycle. If you notice your dishwasher is leaking and you have a suspicion that a damaged gasket is causing it, you can find an OEM dishwasher door gaskets for your GE model, and then read the following guide to assist you in replacing it.
1. Open and lower the door for your dishwasher.
2. Inspect the gasket seal around the perimeter of the dishwasher door. If you notice any rips, tears, holes, or any sort of damage, it will need to be removed and replaced.
3. Pull the old door gasket out from the dishwasher's door frame and dispose of it.
4. With the new gasket in hand, carefully push it into place around the perimeter of the dishwasher door frame.
5. Now run a quick washing cycle and monitor for any leaks.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Clogged Filter in a GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
The filter in your dishwasher, like any other appliance, is there to collect food debris that would otherwise cause issues later on in the draining process. Water sitting at the bottom of your dishwasher after it's finished its washing cycle is a good indication that the filter is clogged, and that could become a leak if not cleaned or replaced. But if you've never changed your GE dishwasher filter and you're now noticing a leak at the bottom or front of it, there's an even greater chance that the filter is causing the leak. Lucky for you, a filter is an incredibly easy part to replace (or clean), and we'll show you precisely how to do it.
1. Turn off the power to your dishwasher.
2. Open your dishwasher door and locate the filter housing at the bottom of the cabinet.
3. Remove the lower spray arm.
4. Twist to remove the old filter. If there's a securing latch, you may need to disengage it before you can remove the filter.
5. Clean the current filter by soaking it for a few minutes, and then washing it by hand with soap. But if there's significant damage to it, replace it with a new filter.
6. Install the new filter by twisting it into place.
7. Reinstall the lower spray arm.
8. Close the dishwasher door and run a quick cycle to test the new filter.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Broken Water Inlet Valve in a GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
A water inlet valve is an electrically controlled valve that is used to regulate and control the water flowing into it, as well as just acting as a gateway for the dishwasher's water supply itself. A broken or shorted water inlet valve will cause leaks in your dishwasher, because it has limited or no control over the flow of water entering it. And since inlet valves are normally located near the bottom of the appliance, it's safe to say that it would be the cause if there's a substantial amount of water around the valve, or underneath near the rear when your dishwasher's off. An easy way to test if the inlet valve is bad, is by opening the door of the dishwasher while it's running – if the water is running, the valve is defective. If your GE dishwasher's inlet valve needs to be replaced, this step-by-step guide will show you exactly how to do that.
1. First, turn off the power and water to the dishwasher, and ensure there is no water on the floor near your appliance.
2. Unthread and disconnect any screws securing the kick plate at the bottom of your dishwasher.
3. Locate the water inlet valve and disconnect the water supply line from it. This may require a wrench to do.
4. De-clamp the drain and fill hose underneath your sink, then unthread any securing screws to the dishwasher.
5. Unthread and disconnect the wires in the junction box before continuing, if necessary.
6. Pull your dishwasher into an open area and rotate it onto its back.
7. Inspect the valve for any signs of damage, breaks or leaks.
8. (Optional) Use a multimeter to test whether the solenoid (part that opens and closes it) has continuity, or whether it's bad.
9. Unscrew and disconnect the valve and its wire harness to remove it.
10. Install the new inlet valve by securing it with screws and connecting the wire harness.
11. Rotate the dishwasher back upright and push it back into place.
12. Connect the water supply line to the valve, and clamp the hoses back into place.
13. If the junction box was disconnected previously, reconnect all of the wires.
14. Plug your dishwasher back in and run short washing cycles and monitor it for leaks.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Float and Float Switch in a GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
The float and float switch, also known as a flood switch, in a GE dishwasher are necessary for detecting and managing the level of water inside the dishwasher during the washing cycle by turning the drain pump on and off. The float will rise and lower depending on the level of water in the dishwasher, but if it gets stuck in either the 'on' or 'off' position (up or down), the pump will either stay on indefinitely or not turn on at all – which is where a leak would arise. So if your GE dishwasher float switch is defective or broken, and you've got a leak underneath your dishwasher, not only do we have the parts you need, we'll tell you how to replace it, too!
1. First, disconnect power to the dishwasher by unplugging it from the wall outlet, turn off the water supply, and remove the racks within the interior of the dishwasher.
2. Remove the lower spray arm.
3. Remove any filters from the bottom of the dishwasher to gain access to the float switch.
4. You may need a screwdriver to unthread and disconnect certain panels within the dishwasher assembly.
5. Once the float switch is accessible, carefully pull it out and disconnect any wires attached to it.
6. Now, you can completely remove the float switch and test it with a multimeter if you'd like.
7. To install the new float switch, connect the wire harness to it and install it within the dishwasher.
8. Reconnect any panels necessary and secure them properly.
9. Reseat the filters and the spray arms, as well as replacing the racks within the dishwasher.
10. Run a quick cycle within the dishwasher and monitor for any leaks.

sections.heading: How to Change a Pump in a GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
The pump in any dishwasher is simply used to circulate and drain water during its washing cycle, and without it working properly or if it's damaged, it will cause excessive water to build up and/or simply leak. An easy way to detect if your drain pump is out of commission is to see if it actually runs during the drain cycle. If it simply hums quietly when it should be draining, it needs to be replaced. However, if it runs and you're still noticing water left in the dishwasher after the cycle is over, your issue likely lies with the drain hose. So if you're finding water underneath your dishwasher, we have a wide-range of GE dishwasher pumps for you to choose from, and a replacement guide to assist you in replacing it!
1. Unplug and disconnect your dishwasher's power, and turn off and disconnect the water supply.
2. Open your dishwasher's door and remove all of the interior contents, including spray arms and filters.
3. Unthread any screws securing the kick plate of your dishwasher.
4. Unthread any securing screws holding your dishwasher in place.
5. Unscrew and disconnect the wires in the junction box before pulling your dishwasher into an open area, and rotating it on its back.
6. Take pictures of any and all wire harnesses for future reference.
7. Inspect the drain pump and the seals for any damage, cracks, or indication of leaks. Replace it if it's damaged.
8. Disconnect all wires and sensors connected to it, then loosen and remove the drain hose.
9. If your model has pump latches, disconnect them.
10. Remove the pump assembly from underneath or through the inside of the cabinet.
11. Now, carefully remove the drain pump motor.
12. Install the new drain pump, and any seals or clamps necessary.
13. Use a small amount of dish soap to lubricate the sump seal, and set it into the dishwasher.
14. Rotate the dishwasher onto its back and secure the sump assembly.
15. Reconnect the drain hose, as well as all wires and sensors to the assembly.
16. Push your dishwasher back into place, and reconnect any wires.
17. Reconnect the water line, kick plate, filter, spray arm and dish racks to the dishwasher.
18. Run a quick cycle and monitor for leaks.

sections.heading: How to Replace a GE Dishwasher Drain or Fill Hose
sections.text:
A clogged, broken or cracked dishwasher hose can be a leading cause for why your dishwasher is leaking and why you're discovering water at the bottom of it. Fill and drain hoses are meant to transport water in and out of the dishwasher, and if they're cracked, clogged, or simply broken, they will eventually leak and cause damage in your home. But finding the right dishwasher hose is simple enough with our wide range of OEM GE dishwasher parts, and we'll even show you exactly how to replace it!
1. First, unplug your dishwasher from the wall outlet and turn off and disconnect the water supply.
2. Unthread and remove the kick plate at the bottom of your dishwasher.
3. Unthread and disconnect the wires in the junction box before continuing, if necessary.
4. Disconnect the drain hose from the sink, and unthread any screws securing the dishwasher.
5. Carefully pull the dishwasher into an open area and rotate the dishwasher onto its back.
6. Locate the drain hose assembly in the dishwasher, and carefully disconnect it if it's damaged or cracked.
7. Install the new drain hose, ensuring all connections and clamps are secure.
8. Rotate the dishwasher back upright and then push the dishwasher back into place to secure it.
9. Connect the new drain hose to the sink where the previous connection was.
10. Reconnect the any junction box wires, as well as the water supply line to the inlet valve.
11. Secure the kick plate at the bottom of your dishwasher, and turn the water supply back on.
12. Plug your dishwasher back in, and run a quick wash cycle to monitor for leaks.

sections.heading: How to Prevent Future Leaks in Your GE Dishwasher
sections.text:
It's important that your GE dishwasher is equipped and in its best condition to ensure that maintenance issues, like leaks, don't happen – or at the very least, not very often. And dishwashers are only as effective at cleaning our dishes as we allow them to be, so these are the most important things you can do to ensure your dishwasher does not leak and gets your dishes clean:
• Use Correct Detergent: An extremely overlooked aspect of dishwashing is using the right detergent; using the wrong type can cause overflow of water and soap, and result in a nasty leak.
• Clean or New Drain Hose: Even though it's a part we mentioned replacing, maintaining a clean drain hose or replacing it when it's clogged or nearing the end of its life cycle will prevent water buildups and leaks.
Now that you hopefully have your dishwasher back in order, you're already on the road to getting clean dishes without the worry of flooding your home! title: How to Fix a Torn Refrigerator Door Seal

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• How to Clean a Refrigerator Door Seal
• How to Repair a Torn Refrigerator Door Seal
• How to Replace a Torn Refrigerator Door Seal
The refrigerator door seal is a flexible strip of rubber that sits along the edge of the fridge door. It is an airtight seal that prevents cold air from escaping the refrigerator and keeps warm air from entering. If the door seal becomes torn, loose, or dirty, your refrigerator will be unable to cool properly, and your food may eventually become spoiled. The refrigerator will also consume more energy as it has to work harder to maintain the correct temperatures, leading to premature wear and increased energy bills. Finally, if your door seal is faulty, you will also likely notice increased condensation on the interior walls of the refrigerator as well as on your food. Therefore, it is important to fix any tears promptly, perform regular cleaning, or replace the door seal if it is no longer in good working condition.

sections.heading: How to Check for Door Seal Failure
Visual Inspection
sections.text:
1. Close the refrigerator door and carefully examine the seal around the entire perimeter of the door.
2. Look for any visible gaps or areas where the seal is not making full contact with the refrigerator cabinet.
3. Check for signs of damage such as tears, cracks, or deformities in the seal.

sections.heading: Dollar Bill Test
sections.text:
1. Open the refrigerator door and place a dollar bill (or any thin piece of paper) between the door seal and the refrigerator cabinet.
2. Close the door on the dollar bill, ensuring that it is held firmly in place by the seal.
3. Try to pull the dollar bill out from between the seal and the refrigerator cabinet. If you can easily remove the dollar bill without much resistance, it indicates that there is an air gap or leak in the seal.

sections.heading: How to Clean a Refrigerator Door Seal
sections.text:
Food particles, debris, and dirt can accumulate on the surface of the door seal over time. As these contaminants build up, they can cause the seal to become stiff and less flexible. A less flexible seal may not be able to fit properly along the refrigerator door, resulting in gaps or air leaks when the door is closed. Build-up on the door seal may also lead to increased wear and tear. Therefore, if you are having difficulties with your door seal, it is recommended to begin by thoroughly cleaning the seal.
1. Mix a solution of mild detergent or cleaner with warm water in a bucket. Avoid using harsh chemicals as they may damage the seal.
2. Dip a soft sponge or cloth into the cleaning solution and gently wipe the entire surface of the door seal until all stains and build-up are removed.
3. After cleaning, rinse the door seal thoroughly with clean water to remove any remaining detergent or cleaner residue.
4. Use a clean, dry cloth to wipe the door seal. Ensure that the seal is completely dry as any remaining moisture can lead to the growth of mold.
5. Close the refrigerator door and test the seal to ensure that it closes properly and creates an airtight seal.

sections.heading: How to Repair a Torn Refrigerator Door Seal
sections.text:
If your door seal has tears or cracks, you can repair these using silicone glue. It is a professional colorless sealant and it is a popular choice for door seals. You can also utilize PVC glue which is a transparent sealant with a shorter drying time than other glues. It is important to note that using sealants to fix tears in your door seal is a temporary measure and it is best to replace the door seal as a more permanent solution.
1. Clean the torn area of the fridge door seal and ensure the cleaned area is completely dry before beginning.
2. Cut a piece of wax paper that is slightly larger than the torn area of the seal.
3. Squeeze a small amount of silicone glue onto the torn area of the seal and spread it evenly over the tear.
4. Carefully place the wax paper over the silicone glue and press it gently into place.
5. Use your fingers to smooth out any air bubbles or wrinkles in the wax paper and ensure that it is lying flat over the sealant.
6. Let the silicone sealant cure according to the manufacturer's instructions. This typically takes several hours.
7. Once the silicone sealant is fully cured, carefully peel away the wax paper from the repaired area.
8. Check the repaired area to ensure that the silicone sealant has formed a strong bond and sealed the tear effectively.
9. Close the refrigerator door and check that the repaired seal creates an airtight seal.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Torn Refrigerator Door Seal
sections.text:
1. Before beginning the repair, first prepare your new door seal for installation by soaking it in warm water for a few hours or using a hair dryer to soften it. This will make it more pliable and easier to install.
2. Start at one corner and gently pull the old door seal away from the refrigerator door. You may need to use a putty knife to help pry the seal off.
3. Use a mild detergent and warm water to clean the area where the old seal was attached to ensure a clean surface for attaching the new seal.
4. Starting at one corner again, press the new door seal into place along the edge of the refrigerator door.
5. Work your way around the entire perimeter, pressing the seal firmly against the door to ensure a tight fit. Make sure the seal is properly aligned and fully seated in the groove around the door.
6. Close the refrigerator door and check for any gaps or areas where the seal is not making proper contact with the refrigerator cabinet. Adjust the seal as needed.
7. After installing the new door seal, allow it to settle into place and conform to the shape of the refrigerator door. This may take a few hours.
8. Once the new seal has settled, check that the refrigerator door closes properly and creates an airtight seal.
By following the steps outlined in this article, you can quickly and effectively repair your refrigerator door seal. From cleaning and inspecting the seal for damage to using temporary repair methods like silicone sealant and wax paper, there are several ways to deal with common issues with fridge door seals. However, it's important to note that while these repairs can be helpful, replacing a damaged seal with a new one is often the best long-term solution for your refrigerator.

title: How to Quickly Fix the Maytag Washer LF Error Code

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• +
Water Supply Taps are Closed
• +
Incorrectly Installed Drain Hose
• +
Faulty Inlet Hoses
• +
Clogged Water Inlet Filters
• +
Faulty Water Inlet Valve
• How to Test Water Pressure Levels for Your Maytag Washer
The LF error code on a Maytag washer stands for "Long Fill". This means that the washer is taking too long to fill with water or not filling at all. The code may also be displayed as F8 E1 or Lo FL depending on your washer model, however, they mean the same thing. The LF error is normally caused by a problem with the water supply, low water pressure, faulty water inlet valves, clogged inlet screens, or an incorrectly installed drain hose. This guide will walk you through identifying and troubleshooting the problem so you can get your washer running again in no time.

sections.heading: Water Supply Taps are Closed
sections.text: Check if the taps supplying water to the washer are fully turned on. The water supply tap is a manual valve typically found on the wall behind the washer. When it is open, it allows water to flow to the washer. If it is not completely open, water will be unable to fill the washer during the wash cycle, resulting in the LF error.

sections.heading: How to Open the Water Taps to Clear the Maytag Washer LF Error
sections.text:
1. Begin by disconnecting the washing machine from the power source.
2. Pull the washer forward if you need to gain better access to the taps.
3. Turn each valve handle or knob in a counterclockwise direction to open it.
4. Check for any leaks around the valve or hoses.
5. If you find that the water pressure is too high or too low, adjust the valve slightly to achieve the desired water flow.
6. Reconnect the washer to the power source and run a short cycle to confirm that the LF code is no longer displayed.

sections.heading: Incorrectly Installed Drain Hose
sections.text: The drain is responsible for carrying water out of the washer at the end of a cycle. However, if it is not properly installed, it can affect the water flowing into the washer. If the end of the drain hose is inserted too far into the standpipe or drain, it will cause a siphoning or vacuum effect. This means that water may continuously drain from the washer, which can prevent the washer from properly filling with water.

sections.heading: How to Correctly Position the Drain Hose to Clear the Maytag Washer LF Error Code
sections.text:
• Adjust Drain Hose Height: The drain hose should be positioned above the water level inside the washer. If it's too low, water can siphon out.
• Install a Standpipe Air Gap: There should be an air gap between the end of the drain hose and the standpipe. If there is no air gap you can purchase one from your local hardware store and install it yourself.
• Use a Drain Hose Restraint: A drain hose restraint keeps the hose secure and can prevent the hose from moving and slipping too far into the standpipe.
• Use the Correct Drain Hose Length: A long hose can increase the chance of kinks and blockages which can affect the flow of water.
• Pull the Washer Forward: Avoid pushing your washer too close to the wall as this may compromise the drain hose. Wherever possible, maintain a straight path for the hose to avoid sharp bends which can restrict water flow.

sections.heading: Faulty Inlet Hoses
sections.text: The inlet hoses are flexible, rubber tubes that connect your washing machine to the water supply. These hoses allow water to flow into the washer for each wash cycle. There is one hose for hot water and one for cold water. If these hoses are kinked or damaged, water will be unable to flow into the washer and fill it up at the appropriate time.

sections.heading: How to Clean and Replace the Inlet Hoses to Clear Maytag Washer LF Error
sections.text:
1. Ensure the washing machine is unplugged from the power outlet to prevent the risk of electric shock.
2. Locate the water supply valves connected to the washing machine and turn them off by turning the handles clockwise. These valves are typically located on the wall behind the washer or under a nearby sink.
3. Carefully pull the washing machine away from the wall to create space to access the back panel.
4. Locate the inlet hoses which are connected to the back of the washing machine. They are usually color-coded, with the hot water hose being red and the cold water hose being blue.
5. Disconnect the hoses from the washer and carefully examine the entire length of each hose for any signs of wear, cracks, or leaks.
6. If you notice any damage, you will need to replace the hose to fix the LF error.
7. Inspect the hoses for any debris or buildup that could restrict water flow and carefully remove any blockages.
8. Once clear, reconnect the hoses to the washing machine and turn on the water supply.
9. Reconnect your washer to power to complete the repair.

sections.heading: Clogged Water Inlet Filters
sections.text: The water inlet filters are protective coverings that prevent dirt and debris from flowing into the washing machine. They are found where the water hoses connect to the back of the washing machine. It is common for these filters to get clogged over time. This buildup restricts the flow of water into the washing machine, reducing the amount of water that enters the tub during the filling cycle and resulting in the LF error. If the filters are excessively clogged, water may not enter the washer at all. It is important to regularly clean them to ensure your washer runs optimally and it is recommended to replace the inlet filters every 6 months. You can browse our selection of Maytag inlet filters if it is time to replace yours.

sections.heading: How to Clean the Water Inlet Filters to Clear the Maytag Washer LF Error Code
sections.text:
1. Ensure the washing machine is unplugged to ensure your safety.
2. Shut off the water supply valves connected to the washing machine to prevent water from flowing while you're working on it.
3. Disconnect the water supply hoses from the back of the washer.
4. Look inside the inlet valves on the back of the washer to locate the mesh filter.
5. Carefully remove the inlet filters. You may need a pair of needle-nose pliers.
6. Run the filters under warm water and use a soft brush to remove any remaining buildup. Once clean, return the filters to their correct positions.
7. If the filters are no longer usable, discard them and install the new ones.
8. Reconnect the water supply hoses and turn on the water supply. Ensure there are no leakages.
9. Turn your washer back on and run a short cycle to check if the code has been cleared.

sections.heading: Faulty Water Inlet Valve
sections.text: The water inlet valve is responsible for controlling the flow of water into the washer. During the wash cycle, the inlet valve opens and allows water to fill the drum. When the correct level of water is reached, the inlet valve closes. If the valve is damaged or faulty it may be unable to allow water to freely flow into the washer. If it is faulty, you must replace the inlet valve to clear the LF error code.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Faulty Water Inlet Valve to Clear the Maytag LF Error Code
sections.text:
1. Unplug the washer, turn off the water supply, and pull the washing machine forward for easier access.
2. Disconnect the water hoses from the back of the washing machine.
3. Remove the back panel of the washer to access the inlet valves.
4. Disconnect the wiring from the water inlet valve.
5. Remove the mounting hardware that secures the valve in place, and carefully pull it out of the washer.
6. Place the new water inlet valve inside the washer and secure it using the appropriate screws.
7. Reconnect the wires to the new valve.
8. Reattach the back panel to the washer and ensure it is fixed in place.
9. Connect each water supply hose to the new inlet valve.
10. Plug the washer back in and test that the new valve is working correctly.

sections.heading: Low Water Pressure
sections.text: The water pressure in your home needs to be adequate for the washer to fill properly. Low water pressure can cause the washer to take longer to fill or not to fill at all. If the valves are open, and there are no leaks in the hoses, you should test your home's water supply using a water pressure test gauge. Typically, water pressure requirements for washing machines range from 20 psi to 120 psi.

sections.heading: How to Test Water Pressure Levels for Your Maytag Washer
sections.text:
1. Identify the water supply valve that provides water to your washing machine. It is usually located on the wall behind the washer or under a sink nearby.
2. Turn off other water fixtures in your home that may be using water, such as faucets, showers, or toilets.
3. Attach the pressure gauge to the water supply valve.
4. Slowly turn on the water supply valve to allow water to flow through the pressure gauge. Monitor the pressure gauge to observe the water pressure reading.
5. Check the pressure reading. If the pressure is low, you may need to call in a plumber or a professional technician to look for any pipe blockages or issues with the plumbing lines.
Encountering the LF error code in your Maytag washer can be frustrating! By first addressing potential problems such as water supply issues or blockages, you can easily troubleshoot your way through this error. However, if you are in doubt it is always best to call in a professional. Remember, regular maintenance, including cleaning water inlet filters and inspecting hoses, is key to optimizing your washer's performance and reducing the chance of any future problems.

title: Why Your Whirlpool Washer Won’t Spin

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post

Troubleshooting and Fixing a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
Whether it's water not draining, clothes remaining soaking wet, or unusual noises during operation, a non-spinning Whirlpool washer may have a defective door latch or lid switch, a displaced drive belt, or a blocked drain hose. In this article, we'll walk you through troubleshooting and fixing these common problems step by step.

sections.heading: Signs Your Whirlpool Washer Isn't Spinning Properly
sections.text:
Dealing with a Whirlpool washer that refuses to spin can be a real head-scratcher. You may notice these warning signs when this happens:
• Water Not Draining: If you find water lingering in the drum after a wash cycle, it's a strong indication that your washer's draining system isn't functioning correctly.
• Clothes Still Soaking Wet: When your freshly washed laundry comes out of your washer dripping wet, it may be linked to an imbalanced load which prevented your washer from wringing out excess water.
• Heavier Loads Aren't Cleaning: If you find that your washer isn't cleaning larger loads properly, it could be because you're using the wrong cycle or your washer isn't sitting level.
• Unusual Noises: Grinding, thumping, or squealing noises during operation can indicate a variety of mechanical issues. For instance, a squealing noise could point to belt problems and clicking might indicate an issue with your washer's lid switch or door lock.
• Silent Spin Cycle: On the other hand, an unusually quiet spin cycle could be due to a malfunctioning lid switch.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and Fixing a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text:
Based on the symptoms you are observing on your non-spinning washer, various underlying reasons may be at play:
• Your Whirlpool Washer Won’t Empty or Spin: It can be frustrating when your washer seems stuck and there's still water inside after a cycle. To tackle this, you’ll need to check the drain hose of your washer to make sure it's not twisted, blocked, or bent in a way that stops the water from getting out.
• Your Whirlpool Washer Drains but Won’t Spin: If your washer is good at getting rid of water but doesn't want to spin, there are two things to check. Look at the lid switch or door latch. If it's engaging, your washer thinks it's not safe to spin. Another possibility is a broken or displaced belt inside the machine.
• Your Whirlpool Washer Does Not Spin at Full Speed: If your washer is spinning slowly or stuttering, it's probably because of heavy or lopsided laundry loads. This can also make your washer move forward during a wash.

sections.heading: Things to Check on a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text: Now that you know the suspects as to why your washer isn’t spinning, it's time to perform some quick troubleshooting. Start by examining these:

sections.heading: Is Your Washer Overloaded?
sections.text: Begin by checking if you've overloaded your washer. Jamming too many clothes inside can hinder the spinning process. To fix this, simply remove some items and try the cycle again.

sections.heading: Are You Selecting the Right Cycle?
sections.text: Using the correct cycle setting also helps the washer adapt to the specific demands of the load, including the spinning process. For example, opt for "bulky" when washing bedding or blankets.

sections.heading: Is Your Washer Level?
sections.text: A balanced washer is crucial for effective spinning. An unlevel washer, with one or more feet not resting evenly on the ground, can lead to spinning problems. Use a level to check the appliance's balance and adjust the legs until the washer sits perfectly horizontal.

sections.heading: How to Troubleshoot the Lid Switch on a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text:
The lid switch in a top load Whirlpool washer is a safety feature that stops the machine from spinning when the lid is open. This small plastic component can be found either under the lid or on the top of the machine. You can manually activate it by gently pushing the tip of a screwdriver into it, to simulate the lid being closed. You should hear a distinct click from the switch whenever you close the lid shut. If you don't hear this click, the switch might need replacement. Follow these steps to inspect and test the lid switch:
1. Begin by disconnecting your washer from the power source.
2. Locate the lid switch, typically situated in the top right corner where the lid would close. On certain models, you might need to remove the top control panel or even the entire washer cabinet to access the lid switch.
3. Take out the screws holding the lid switch in place.
4. Carefully pull the lid switch from its position. The lid switch may still be attached due to wiring and retaining clips. Disconnect and remove these components.
5. To test the lid switch, use a multimeter to check for continuity. If the lid is closed (or you simulate it as closed), the multimeter should display continuity, often indicated by a beep or a reading close to zero ohms. A reading in this range confirms that the switch is functioning correctly. If there's no continuity, it's time to replace the lid switch.

sections.heading: How to Troubleshoot the Door Latch on a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text:
Like the lid switch on top load washers, the latch ensures the door on front load machines is securely locked during operation. It is usually behind the front panel of the washer, near the door frame. It consists of a latch assembly with a locking mechanism that engages with the door strike. If the door is not properly latched, the washer will not operate. This means that if the latch is defective, the washer will not spin. To access and check the door latch:
1. Unplug the washer or turn off the breaker to ensure safety.
2. Open the washer door. You might need to remove the front panel or access panel to reach the latch mechanism.
3. Remove the screws holding the latch assembly in place and lift it off its mounting bracket.
4. Disconnect the wires attached to the door latch assembly, and remove it from the washer. Some models may have a shield over the connectors that can be removed with a flathead screwdriver.
5. Test the door latch with a multimeter by first setting it to the continuity setting.
6. Look at the connector to identify the terminal pins for the door latch. Typically, there will be two or three pins that you'll be testing for continuity.
7. Touch the multimeter probes to the terminal pins on the door latch connector. You may need to refer to your owner's manual to know which pins to test. If testing a two-pin latch, place one probe on each pin. If there are more than two pins, you'll need to consult your washer's wiring diagram to know which pins to test for continuity.
8. If there is no continuity, the latch is defective and needs to be replaced.

sections.heading: How to Troubleshoot the Drive Belt on a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text:
The drive belt in a Whirlpool washer connects the motor to the drum, allowing it to spin. If the belt is worn, stretched, or broken, the drum won't spin properly. Signs of a failing belt include a squealing noise during operation or visible wear on the belt itself.
1. Unplug the washer from the power source, turn off the water supply to the washer, and disconnect the hoses to provide easier access to the rear washer panel.
2. Remove the back panel of the washer.
3. Check that the drive belt is secure and not frayed.
4. If you decide to replace the drive belt, turn the tub drive pulley, and the belt should fall off.
5. To install a new drive belt, put one end of the new belt around the motor pulley and place the other end on the tub drive pulley. Rotate the tub drive pulley to secure the new drive belt.
6. With the new drive belt fitted, reassemble the washer.

sections.heading: How to Troubleshoot the Drain Hose on a Whirlpool Washer That Won’t Spin
sections.text:
A kinked drain hose disrupts the flow of water, preventing your Whirlpool Washer from properly expelling from the washer's drum and unable to move into the spin cycle. To troubleshoot and install the hose correctly:
1. Start by inspecting the drain hose to identify any kinks or bends that might be obstructing water flow.
2. If you spot a kink in the drain hose, loosen the clamp that holds it in place at the washer's connection point. Carefully remove the kinked hose from the washer.
3. Replace the kinked hose with a new one. Ensure that the new drain hose is securely attached to your washer, and tighten the clamp to hold it firmly in place. To further prevent kinks, straighten the drain hose as much as possible.
4. If needed, use a U-shaped drain hose form (often included with the washer or available separately) to maintain the shape and position of the hose.
5. While troubleshooting the drain hose, also examine the drainpipe or utility sink where the hose expels the water. Make sure there are no blockages or clogs that could impede water drainage.
If you've gone through these troubleshooting steps and your Whirlpool washer still refuses to spin, it may be time to seek professional assistance. An experienced technician can diagnose and fix more complex issues, so that your washer can get back to its spinning best.

Frequently Asked Questions About Water Filters
If the water from your LG refrigerator has a funny taste or smell to it, it's likely a sign that the water filter is in dire need of replacing. After all, water filters are used to remove any chemicals or minerals that would be unhealthy to drink, like chlorine, VOCs (volatile organic compounds), and many more. Which is why we're going to show you exactly how to replace an LG refrigerator's water filter, and answer some popular questions along the way.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Different Types of LG Refrigerator Water Filters
sections.text: Although there are quite a few different models and types of LG refrigerators, they all borrow from a shared pool of water filters. Speaking of, you can find the water filter for your LG refrigerator in PartSelect's water filter finder! Each of these filter types all serve the same purpose, in filtering out harsh chemicals, contaminants, and unpleasant tasting minerals, but they all require different ways of removing and installing. Before replacing any water filter, ensure your water line supply is shut and turned off.

sections.heading: Inline Water Filter
sections.text:
Inline water filters are installed outside of your refrigerator and are designed to allow the water line to flow inline through it, on its way to the refrigerator. The most common LG refrigerators that use inline water filters are top freezer models.
1. For this replacement, you will require a bucket and a towel.
2. Locate an inline water filter behind the fridge. It is normally mounted to the wall or the fridge itself.
3. Your filter will have two water lines going into each end of the filter, with a grommet securing each tube. Carefully remove the tubes from each end.
4. Take the new filter and plug the water supply line into one end.
5. Now turn your water supply on and flush 2.5 gallons of water through the filter to flush and prime it. Once finished, turn off the water supply.
6. Then, install the fridge's water line into the filter.
7. To ensure the filter is installed correctly, if you pull slightly on each line, the line should stay inside the filter.
8. Install the filter to your wall or refrigerator mount, and turn on the water supply.

sections.heading: Twist to Remove Water Filter
sections.text:
Twist to remove water filters are normally located in the top left or top right portion of your French 3 or 4 door, side-by-side, or top freezer refrigerator, or in its door.
1. Pull the tray of the water filter out if applicable, and allow the filter to swing out or down.
2. Grab the filter and turn it counterclockwise until it disconnects and comes out of the filter housing.
3. Take the new filter and place it in the filter housing, then rotate it clockwise until it's secure.
4. If your filter has a housing or tray, push it into place and close the housing.
5. Now, turn on the water supply to the refrigerator and dispense 2.5 gallons of water to flush and prime the filter.

sections.heading: Pull Down Water Filter
sections.text:
If your refrigerator has a pull down water filter, you will normally locate it in French 3 or 4 door, or side-by-side models of refrigerators.
1. Locate the water filter in the top right or top left of the refrigerator cabinet.
2. Open the water filter tray, and the water filter should swing out.
3. Pull the water filter down carefully and it should simply come out.
4. With your new water filter in hand, push it into the filter housing, and swing it upwards towards the fridge ceiling.
5. Close the water filter tray, and turn on the water supply.
6. Flush 2.5 gallons of water through the water dispenser to get the filter primed and ready to be used.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Water Filters
sections.text: When replacing the water filter in your LG refrigerator, there are some common misconceptions and things that are popularly misunderstood - and we're hoping that these frequently asked questions will clear up anything you're curious about!

sections.heading: Are generic water filters OK to use?
sections.text: Generic and non-OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) filters are not suitable for use for most appliances and equipment, especially not refrigerators. OEM water filters require much less maintenance, are designed to work specifically with your refrigerator model, and because they are made and supplied directly from the original manufacturer, and thus go through the same quality testing, they also typically last much longer.

sections.heading: How often do I need to change my LG refrigerator's water filter?
sections.text: You need to replace your LG refrigerator's water filter once every 6 months, or as needed. It's important to look for taste differences in the water, an indicator that will light around the time the filter needs to be replaced, or a significantly lower level of water pressure from the dispenser.

sections.heading: Can you replace an LG refrigerator water filter without turning off water?
sections.text: When replacing the water filter for your LG refrigerator, it's important to disengage and turn off the water line to ensure a large amount of excess water does not come out from the water filter port when replacing it.

sections.heading: How do I reset my LG refrigerator after installing a new water filter?
sections.text:
Once your water filter for your LG refrigerator has been replaced with a new one, you can easily reset the water filter light indicator by holding the 'Reset Filter' button for 3-5 seconds, until the light turns off.
Now that you've replaced the water filter in your LG refrigerator, you're able to enjoy tasty and contaminant-free water! Remember that water filters need to replaced on a regular basis, and at the very most should be replaced after 6-8 months of regular use. However, if you use your refrigerator's built-in water dispenser more or less often than average, you may be looking at a different lifespan for your new filter.

title: Why is My Whirlpool Washer Stuck on Sensing?

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• Faulty Whirlpool Washer Shift Actuator
• +
Clogged Whirlpool Washer Drain Pump
• +
Faulty Whirlpool Washer Pressure Switch
• Faulty Door Latch
• +
Faulty Whirlpool Washer Lid Switch
• +
Faulty Whirlpool Washer Drive Belt
• How to Reset Your Whirlpool Washer
The most common cause of a Whirlpool washer that is stuck on sensing is a faulty actuator. However, this problem may also be caused by a clogged drain pump, a failed door latch/lid switch, a torn drive belt, a faulty pressure switch, or faulty water inlet valves. The sensing function on a Whirlpool washer detects the size of the laundry load and adjusts the amount of water in the washer accordingly. If your washer is stuck on this sensing cycle, it will be unable to advance through the rest of the cycles and clean your laundry. This guide will show you how to troubleshoot these faulty parts and get your washer running normally again.

sections.heading: Faulty Whirlpool Washer Shift Actuator
sections.text: The shift actuator is responsible for controlling the movement of the washer's agitator and spin basket during the wash cycle. It ensures that the washer switches between washing, spinning, and other cycles smoothly. If the shift actuator is faulty, it will be unable to move through the cycles and may leave your washer stuck on one cycle, such as the sensing cycle. You will need to replace the shift actuator to fix your washer.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Shift Actuator to Fix a Washer Stuck on Sensing
sections.text:
1. Ensure the washer is unplugged from the electrical outlet to guarantee your safety while working on it.
2. Turn off the water supply to the washer and disconnect the hoses.
3. Depending on your model, there might be screws at the back or end caps that need to be removed to release the control panel.
4. Lift the control panel and locate the actuator. It's typically positioned near the motor.
5. Disconnect any wires attached to the actuator, making a note of their positions for reassembly.
6. Remove any mounting screws securing the actuator to the washer.
7. Install the new shift actuator in the same position and secure it with the mounting screws.
8. Reconnect the wires to the appropriate terminals.
9. Put the control panel back in place and secure it with screws or clips.
10. Reconnect the water supply hoses.
11. Plug the washer back in and run a test cycle to ensure that the new shift actuator is functioning correctly.

sections.heading: Clogged Whirlpool Washer Drain Pump
sections.text: The drain pump is responsible for removing wastewater from your washing machine through the drain hose and into the drainpipe or washtub. If the drain pump is clogged, the washer cannot advance through its cycles, thus leaving your washer stuck on sensing. To fix this issue you will need to remove any obstructions that may be blocking the drain pump.

sections.heading: How To Access and Clean the Drain Pump in a Whirlpool Washer
sections.text:
1. Disconnect your washing machine from the power outlet.
2. Depending on your washer model, you may need to either remove the back panel of your washer to access your drain pump or you may need to remove the console and front panel. Check your user manual for the exact specifications.
3. Locate the drain pump at the bottom of the washer, near the front or rear side, and place a bucket or towel underneath the pump area.
4. Disconnect the hoses connected to the drain pump. It is normal for water to spill out at this point.
5. Remove the mounting fasteners that secure the drain pump to the washer and pull it out.
6. Remove and clean the pump filter if your model has one. Simply place it under warm rushing water to clear it of any debris.
7. Inspect the inside of the pump housing for any debris or small/loose items such as coins or buttons.
8. Inspect the pump impeller for any obstructions and ensure it can rotate freely.
9. Once you are done, place the filter back onto the pump and return it to the washer.
10. Secure the pump in place and reattach the hoses.
11. Reassemble your washer in reverse order and run a short cycle to check that your washer is now functioning properly.

sections.heading: Faulty Whirlpool Washer Pressure Switch
sections.text: The pressure switch helps to detect when the washer is sufficiently filled with water. It tells the control panel when it is time to start flushing out the water and tells the control board when the machine is empty, so that the spin cycle may begin. If the pressure switch experiences electrical issues or is physically damaged the washer will be unable to detect when it is time to advance to the next cycle. You will need to find a new pressure switch to replace the faulty one.

sections.heading: How To Test and Replace the Pressure Switch in a Washer Stuck on Sensing
sections.text:
1. Unplug your washer and turn off the water supply.
2. Locate the pressure switch. It is typically found either under the control panel or under the top panel of your washer.
3. Remove the air pressure tube from the old pressure switch gently, using a pair of pliers.
4. Disconnect the wire harness from the pressure switch and remove the screws holding the switch in place.
5. Inspect the switch for signs of damage and replace it if necessary.
6. If there is no damage, you should test the pressure switch for continuity.
7. Set your multimeter to the lowest setting or “ohms” setting.
8. Connect the prongs on your multimeter to the two outside terminals.
9. Blow into the hose to create pressure and check the reading on the meter. The reading should be close to “0”. If it is out of range, then the pressure switch will need to be replaced.
10. Take your new pressure switch and place it in the same position as the old one.
11. Reconnect the wire harness and secure the switch using the mounting screws.
12. Reattach the air pressure tube and reassemble your washer.

sections.heading: Faulty Whirlpool Washer Water Inlet Valve
sections.text: The water inlet valve controls the flow of water into the washing machine drum. If the valves are damaged or faulty, they will be unable to carry out this function. Your washer may remain stuck on the sensing cycle because it is unable to adjust the water levels in the washer due to the failure of the water valves. Browse our selection of genuine Whirlpool OEM water inlet valves to find a new one for your washer.

sections.heading: How to Replace a Faulty Water Inlet Valve in a Washer Stuck on Sensing
sections.text:
1. Disconnect the washing machine from the electrical outlet, and turn off the water supply.
2. Pull the washing machine away from the wall.
3. Disconnect the water hoses from the back of the washing machine.
4. Remove the rear panel of the washer and disconnect the wiring from the faulty water inlet valve.
5. Remove the mounting fasteners holding the valve in place, and carefully pull it out of the washer.
6. Mount the new valve in place and secure it using the appropriate screws.
7. Reconnect the wiring to the new valve and reassemble the washer in reverse order.
8. Reconnect the water hoses to the new valve, and ensure each hose is in the right position.
9. Restore the power to your washer and check whether it is properly functioning.

sections.heading: Faulty Door Latch
sections.text: The door latch is responsible for keeping the washer door shut. When the door is closed, it engages with the strike, which communicates to the washer that it is safe to begin a cycle. If the door is unable to stay closed or communicate that it is closed, your washer may stop mid-cycle or fail to start altogether. You can explore our genuine OEM Whirlpool door latches here.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Door Latch to Fix a Washer Stuck on Sensing
sections.text:
1. Disconnect the washer from the power outlet.
2. Open the washer door and carefully peel the door boot off the washer frame.
3. Undo the mounting fasteners that hold the door latch in place. If it is damaged, it will need to be replaced.
4. If there is no visible damage, use a multimeter to test the switch for potential electrical failure.
5. If you find that the latch should be replaced, simply discard the old one and position the new one over the mounting holes.
6. Reconnect the wire harness and secure the new latch in place.
7. Remember to return the door boot to the washer before closing the door to test that the latch is functional.

sections.heading: Faulty Whirlpool Washer Lid Switch
sections.text: The lid switch is a safety mechanism found under the washer lid that. It is responsible for ensuring that the washer lid is securely shut so that the wash cycle can begin. If the lid switch is damaged or faulty the washer may not start, spin, drain or it may remain stuck on the sensing cycle, unable to advance. You will need to find a new pressure switch to replace the faulty one.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Lid Switch in a Washer Stuck on Sensing
sections.text:
1. Disconnect the washer from the power outlet.
2. Take a putty knife and slide it under the top panel of the washer to release the clips the hold the lid in position.
3. Carefully pull the top panel up and rest it against the washer.
4. Disconnect the wiring harness. It may be helpful to take an image of how the wires are routed for reinstallation later.
5. Inspect the switch for any physical damage and test the switch for continuity using a multimeter.
6. Once you have established that the switch needs to be replaced, you can remove it from the washer and discard it.
7. Place the new switch on the underside of the cabinet and secure it with the appropriate fasteners.
8. Reattach the wiring harness using your image from earlier.
9. Return the top panel of the cabinet to the washer.
10. Reconnect the washer to the power outlet and check that it is now working.

sections.heading: Faulty Whirlpool Washer Drive Belt
sections.text:
The drive belt is a thin rubber strip that connects the motor to the drum, allowing it to spin. If the belt is frayed, loose or broken, it will be unable to transfer the power from the motor to the drum. The drum may not spin at all or become stuck on a cycle. You will need to replace the drive belt to restore your washer's functions.
1. Unplug the washer from the power source, and turn off the water supply to the washer.
2. Disconnect the water supply hoses from the back of the washer.
3. Remove the fasteners along the back panel of the washer and pull the panel off.
4. Inspect the drive belt to verify whether it is in good condition. Replace the belt if it can no longer maintain tension or it is visibly cracked.
5. Rotate the tub drive pulley to release the old belt.
6. Loop the new belt around the motor pulley and place the other end on the tub drive pulley. Ensure that the grooved side is facing inwards.
7. Rotate the tub drive pulley to secure the new drive belt.
8. Reassemble the washer in reverse order and reconnect the water supply hoses.

sections.heading: How to Reset Your Whirlpool Washer
sections.text:
Your washer may be stuck on the sensing cycle due to a control board error. If you have tried the steps above and your washer is still not working you can follow the steps below to reset your washer.
1. Disconnect the washing machine from the power outlet. To perform a hard reset, you can also turn it off at the circuit breaker.
2. Leave the washing machine unplugged for 3 - 5 minutes.
3. Reconnect the washer to the power outlet and turn it on at the circuit breaker.
4. Run a short cycle to check that the washer is now working. If you would like more detailed instructions on how to reset your washer, follow our Whirlpool reset guide.
We know how frustrating it can be when you can't do your laundry. Following the guide above should help you to fix your washer and allow it to advance past the sensing cycle. Remember, regular maintenance and cleaning will help keep your Whirlpool washer running efficiently for many more years.

title: How to Reset an LG Washer with an LE Error Code

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:

How to Clear an LE Error Code on an LG Washer
• +
Parts to Inspect on Your LG Washer
Front-load washers offer many advantages over a top-load machine, such as their increased load capacity while being more energy efficient. The tumbling motion provides a more thorough clean while being gentler on your clothes than an agitator. Despite how hard working your front-load washer is, it isn’t invincible! Overloading the machine can cause strain on the motor and may result in you seeing an LE error code on the display. When this happens, it means that the tub can’t spin due to an issue with the motor. The machine may just be overloaded, or an object has caused a jam preventing the tub from spinning. We'll walk you through the steps to clear the LE error code from your LG washer, along with the parts you may need to inspect or replace on your machine.

sections.heading: How to Clear an LE Error Code on an LG Washer
sections.text:
To clear the LE error code, start by doing a hard reset of the machine.
1. Begin by turning off the washer and then unplugging the power cord.
2. Wait at least 5 minutes, then plug the machine back in.
3. The code should now be cleared from the display.
4. Start the wash cycle again, if the error code returns, follow the next steps below.

sections.heading: Remove Excess Items from the Washer
sections.text:
If you reset your washer, started a new cycle, and the LE error code came back, then your washer may be overloaded. Remove some of the laundry from your washer, reset the machine, and try the cycle again. If the error code comes back again, there may be a lodged item preventing the tub from spinning.
Constantly overloading your washer will strain the motor and can damage it to the point of failure. Be mindful when filling the machine, and if your LG washer has the option, select the “bedding cycle” when washing blankets or bulkier items. An oversized load should be taken to a commercial laundromat, as they have larger machines equipped for that purpose. Spending the time and money to run two smaller loads, or taking an oversized one to a laundromat, will ultimately save you in the long run as it reduced the wear and tear on your washer.

sections.heading: Remove Foreign Objects
sections.text:
If the LE error code comes back again after removing excess laundry from your machine, there may be an object stuck which is preventing the drum from spinning. Remove all the laundry from the machine and see if you can manually turn the tub. If you find an object, remove it from the machine using pliers or tweezers if necessary.
To prevent this from happening in the future, inspect your clothing prior to loading the machine. Spare change, loose buttons, bra underwires, or objects like paperclips can all get lodged in your washer.
If there wasn’t anything stuck in your washer tub, but the error code is still persistent, the motor components may have been damaged and will need to be inspected.

sections.heading: Parts to Inspect on Your LG Washer
sections.text: Constantly overloading your washer puts strain on the motor. This will cause the components to wear faster than normal and require replacement. If you are frequently getting an LE error code on your LG washer, the following motor parts should be inspected. If needed they can replaced with a new OEM motor part.

sections.heading: Rotor
sections.text: The rotor ensures the tub of your washer can spin. It works with the stator to create an electromagnetic field, which in turn causes the tub to rotate. If the magnets on the rotor have become damaged or loose, it can result in your washer not spinning.

sections.heading: How to Access and Remove the Rotor
sections.text:
1. The rotor will be found at the back of your washer. Begin by disconnecting the power and water supply to your machine.
2. Next, remove the back panel to access the rotor.
3. Remove the bolt holding the rotor in place.
4. Once this is removed, you can remove the rotor and inspect it for damage.

sections.heading: How to Install a New Rotor
sections.text:
1. To install a new rotor, line up the opening on the motor shaft and push it into place. You may feel some resistance when lining the new rotor up, as the magnets are engaging with the stator.
2. Once the new rotor is in place, the bolt can be reinstalled and tightened.
3. The back panel can be reinstalled, and the water lines and power reconnected.

sections.heading: Rotor Positioning Sensor
sections.text: The rotor positioning sensor communicates with the electronic control board in your washer to dictate the speed and direction that the tub spins. If the sensor is faulty, it may result in your washer not spinning.

sections.heading: How to Access and Remove the Rotor Positioning Sensor
sections.text:
The rotor positioning sensor is found behind the rotor and is clipped onto the stator.
1. Begin by pulling the washer out from the wall and disconnecting the power and water lines.
2. Remove the back panel of the washer, and the bolt holding the rotor in place.
3. Remove the rotor from the shaft.
4. You may also need to remove the stator from the machine to access the sensor, which can be done by removing the various bolts holding it in place.

sections.heading: How to Install a New Sensor
sections.text:
1. Depending on your model of washer, the sensor and stator may be sold as an assembly or as separate components. If they come as one piece, then the stator will also be replaced if the sensor has failed. If the sensor can be removed, unclip it from the stator and connect the new part in its place.
2. Reinstall and stator onto the shaft and secure the bolts in place.
3. Then replace the rotor by fitting it over top of the stator, and install the bolt.
4. The back panel of the washer can now be reinstalled, and the water lines and power can be reconnected.
You can prevent LE error codes on your LG washer by washing suitable size loads of laundry, selecting the proper cycles, and ensuring that foreign objects don’t make their way into the tub. When problems do occur, we’ve got the repair resources and replacement parts to get your machine back up and running in no time.

title: How to Quickly Clear the LG Dishwasher AE Error Code

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Post
• Pin It
• Share
• Subscribe
• How Using Detergent Incorrectly Can Cause the AE Error
• How an LG Dishwasher That is Not Level Cause the AE Error
• +
How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Door Gasket can Cause the AE Error
• +
How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Float Sensor can Cause the AE Error
• +
How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Spray Arm can Cause the AE Error
• +
How a Faulty Water Inlet Valve can Cause the AE Error
The LG dishwasher AE error code indicates that the float switch has been activated due to a leak in the dishwasher. This error may be displayed as E1 on certain models of LG dishwashers. It may be triggered by a faulty sensor, however it is commonly caused by using too much or incorrect detergent, a control board glitch, a worn-down door gasket, a faulty spray arm, or a faulty water inlet valve. This repair guide is designed to help you find the cause of the issue and troubleshoot it to clear the code and restore your LG dishwasher.

sections.heading: How Using Detergent Incorrectly Can Cause the AE Error
sections.text:
• Use one dishwasher pod per cycle: Your LG dishwasher is designed to use one pod at a time. Using more than one pod can lead to overflow and leaking, resulting in the AE error.
• Use the correct amount of detergent: Ensure that you are following the marked levels for correct amount of detergent to use otherwise you will have excessive suds and cause water to overflow, resulting in the AE error. In LG dishwashers, you should use the 15 Line for slightly dirty loads and the 25 Line for very dirty dishes with stuck-on food.
• Do not use dishwashing liquid: It may be tempting to reach for dishwashing liquid when you are out of pods/tablets, however, dishwashers are not designed for this. Using dishwashing liquid can lead to excessive suds and leaking.

sections.heading: How an LG Dishwasher That is Not Level Cause the AE Error
sections.text: If your dishwasher is not level, water will not drain from the appliance. This can lead to overflow and leaking which triggers the AE error. Your dishwasher must be level for it to function properly. You can check whether it is level by placing a bubble level on the dishwasher door. The bubble should be centred within the lines and if it is not that is a signal that the appliance is not level. You can also pour water on the bottom of the dishwasher and check whether it pools to one side. If it does, this is also a signal that the washer is not level. To balance your dishwasher, you should firstly make sure that it is resting on a flat, even surface. If this does not resolve the issue, you will need to adjust the levelling legs which are found on the underside of the appliance. Turn the legs clockwise to raise their height and counterclockwise to lower them.

sections.heading: How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Door Gasket can Cause the AE Error
sections.text: The door gasket is responsible for creating a watertight seal between the dishwasher door and tub. It prevents water from leaking out during use. It's typically made of rubber and you can find it around the perimeter of the dishwasher door. Over time, the door gasket may wear out or become damaged. If it has failed, you will need to find a replacement door gasket in order to clear the AE error. It is also possible for food and soap residue to build up on the door gaskets resulting in leakages and thereby causing the AE Error.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Door Gasket in Your LG Dishwasher
sections.text:
1. Open the dishwasher door and make note of how the old gasket is installed to help you position the new one later.
2. Carefully peel off the old gasket from around the perimeter of the dishwasher door.
3. Thoroughly clean the area where the old gasket was installed. It may be helpful to use a gentle soap or a mixture of water and vinegar to remove any stubborn residue.
4. Starting at one corner, press the new gasket in place, making sure it fits snugly all the way around. If the new gasket seems stiff, you can soak it in warm water for a few minutes before installation to make it softer.
5. Make sure the gasket is properly aligned and fully seated against the door.
6. Close the dishwasher door and check that it is properly aligned and tightly sealed.
7. Plug the dishwasher back into the power supply.
8. Run a short test cycle to ensure that the door gasket is working effectively. Check for any leaks during the cycle.

sections.heading: How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Float Sensor can Cause the AE Error
sections.text: The float sensor is designed to monitor and control the water level inside the dishwasher. When you start a wash cycle, the dishwasher begins to fill with water and the float sensor helps monitor this process to avoid overfilling. The float sensor can trigger an alert or shut off the water supply incase of a leak or drainage issue. It is found at the bottom of the dishwasher's tub. Once the float reaches a certain level, the float sensor signals the dishwasher's water inlet valve to stop the flow of water. If it is faulty or damaged the sensor may be unable to detect the correct water levels thus resulting in the AE error.

sections.heading: How to Test the Float Sensor
sections.text:
1. Depending on your dishwasher model, you may need to remove the bottom front panel or you may be able to access the float sensor from inside the dishwasher.
2. The float sensor is typically a small, plastic device that moves up and down with the water level. It is often located near the front or side of the dishwasher's interior.
3. Carefully disconnect any wires connected to the float sensor.
4. Set your multimeter to the continuity mode, and touch the multimeter probes to the terminals of the float sensor.
5. If the multimeter beeps this indicates that the circuit is closed, and the float sensor is functioning correctly.
6. If there is no beep, then the circuit is open, and the float sensor is likely faulty.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Float Sensor in Your LG Dishwasher
sections.text:
1. Unplug the dishwasher from the electrical outlet or turn off the circuit breaker.
2. Depending on your dishwasher model, you may need to remove the lower access panel at the front.
3. Identify the float sensor and carefully disconnect any wiring or connectors attached to the float sensor.
4. Remove any fasteners holding the float sensor in place and gently lift it out.
5. Place the new float sensor in the same position as the old one and secure it in place.
6. Reconnect any wiring or connectors to the new float sensor.
7. Put the lower access panel back in place and secure it with screws.
8. Plug the dishwasher back into the electrical outlet or turn the circuit breaker back on.
9. Run a test cycle to ensure that the new float sensor is functioning correctly and the AE code has been cleared.

sections.heading: How a Faulty LG Dishwasher Spray Arm can Cause the AE Error
sections.text: The spray arm distributes water throughout the dishwasher to rinse off and remove food particles and debris from the dishes. If the spray arm has any blockages or clogs, it may not distribute water evenly during the wash cycle. This can lead to an imbalance of water within the dishwasher, causing leaks. A damaged or warped spray arm may not spin properly, leading to uneven water distribution. This can result in water pooling in certain areas of the dishwasher, potentially causing leaks. If the spray arm itself has cracks or holes, water may escape from these openings, causing leaks.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Spray Arm in an LG Dishwasher
sections.text:
1. Begin by disconnecting the dishwasher from the power outlet.
2. Open the dishwasher door and pull out the lower rack.
3. The spray arm is typically located on the bottom of the dishwasher.
4. In some dishwashers the spray arm is secured by a locking mechanism and in others it is a nut. If it has a locking mechanism, release it by turning it counterclockwise. If there is a nut, use the appropriate tool to unscrew it.
5. Take the new spray arm and attach it in the same position where you removed the old one.
6. Secure it by tightening the locking mechanism or nut.
7. Slide the lower rack back into the dishwasher.
8. Reconnect the power to the dishwasher and turn on the water supply.
9. Run a short test cycle to ensure that the new spray arm is working correctly. Check for any leaks or unusual noises.

sections.heading: How a Faulty Water Inlet Valve can Cause the AE Error
sections.text: The water inlet valve controls the flow of water into the dishwasher during usage. It allows water to enter during different cycles such as for tasks such as filling the tub, and rinsing. If the water inlet valve is faulty or malfunctioning, it can lead to inadequate water supply, overflow, or leakage which triggers the AE error code.

sections.heading: How to Replace the Water Inlet Valve in an LG Dishwasher
sections.text:
1. Disconnect the dishwasher from the power source and shut off the water supply to the dishwasher.
2. Remove the kick plate at the bottom of the dishwasher to access the valve.
3. Carefully disconnect the water supply line from the water inlet valve. It is recommended to have a container or towel nearby as water may spill out at this point.
4. Carefully disconnect the electrical wires connected to the water inlet valve. Take note of their positions or take a picture for reference during reinstallation.
5. Remove the mounting hardware that holds the water inlet valve in place, and carefully detach the valve from the dishwasher.
6. Position the new water inlet valve in place and secure it with the screws.
7. Reconnect the electrical wires using your notes/image from earlier.
8. Reattach the water supply line to the new water inlet valve.
9. Turn on the water supply and restore power to the dishwasher.
10. Check that the new valve is working by running a short cycle.
11. Monitor the dishwasher for any leaks and ensure that the AE code has been cleared.
Understanding the various causes behind the AE error code will help you to quickly and easily clear the code and restore your dishwasher. By following the proper use instructions for your dishwasher as well as performing regular maintenance, you will be able to avoid this error code and keep your dishwasher running for longer. If you are in need of new LG dishwasher parts for your appliance, you can browse our wide selection of OEM replacement parts. However, if the error code is still displayed after following the troubleshooting instructions above then it is recommended to consult a repair technician or contact LG customer service.
